# Halve bulletSpeed in unknown-archetype fallbacks

## Problem statement

AH-0MUWZ5GST003NMFQ halves the enemy `bulletSpeed` of the eight shipped archetypes
across the runtime CSV, `DEFAULT_ENEMY_CONFIGS` and the per-entity constants.
During planning, three additional runtime fallbacks were found that also hard-code
`bulletSpeed: 200` for **unknown** archetype keys and were explicitly out of that
item's scope (its Q2 enumeration covered only CSV + defaults + entity constants):

- `src/core/configStore.ts` — `genericEnemyDefault()`
- `src/core/difficultySequencer.ts` — `resolveBaseConfig()`
- `src/core/enemyDifficulty.ts` — `groupEnemyConfig()`

Leaving them at 200 means an unknown-key enemy would fire at double the speed of
every shipped archetype, so tuning can still drift for that edge case.

## Desired change

Decide and, if accepted, halve these three `bulletSpeed` fallbacks (200 → 100) for
consistency, updating any affected difficulty-sequencer expectations.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC1 — The three unknown-archetype fallbacks use `bulletSpeed: 100` (or a
  documented decision is recorded to leave them at 200 with rationale).
- [ ] AC2 — Any difficulty-sequencer or difficulty-scoring test affected by the
  change is updated and the full suite passes.
- [ ] AC3 — The decision and rationale are recorded on this item.

## Key Files

- `src/core/configStore.ts`
- `src/core/difficultySequencer.ts`
- `src/core/enemyDifficulty.ts`

## Related work

- AH-0MUWZ5GST003NMFQ — Reduce bullet speed of enemies (parent discovery; strictly out of its scope).
data.title: Halve bulletSpeed in unknown-archetype fallbacks

discovered-from:AH-0MUYRJQE50021T4A

## Problem

Several deterministic bot micro-simulations are knife-edge calibrations: a subtle, legitimate gameplay tweak (e.g. the 1-5% gentler thrust-press reduction in AH-0MUYRJQE50021T4A) flips their outcomes because scores are dominated by discrete hit/bullet collisions.

During AH-0MUYRJQE50021T4A two tests had to be recalibrated:
- src/ai/style/evaluation.test.ts - synthetic human seed moved 7 -> 14.
- src/ai/framework/competent/competentBot.integration.test.ts - RUN_SEED moved 0x0b07 -> 0x0b16.

On the base behaviour, src/ai/style/evaluation.test.ts already regressed on 13/24 seeds, and the competent-vs-legacy AC6 test only wins in base because the legacy bot chaotically collides with bullets; without bullets the legacy bot scored higher (22 vs 20) on base.

## Goal

Make these tests robust rather than seed-picked:
- Aggregate competence/style comparisons over a set of seeds (e.g. assert the styled/competent bot is not systematically worse), or
- Compare on scenarios whose score is not dominated by discrete collisions.

## Acceptance criteria

- AC1: The style-match AC4 demonstration no longer depends on a single lucky seed (e.g. asserts over multiple seeds).
- AC2: The competent-vs-legacy AC6 test asserts an objective-based advantage rather than relying on chaotic bullet collisions.
- AC3: Recalibrating either test is not required by an unrelated small bot-feel tweak.
- AC4: Full test suite, typecheck and build pass.
data.title: Make bot micro-simulation tests robust to small feel tweaks

**discovered-from:AH-0MVF6Y29M005TEOG** (epic AH-0MVF3BESP005ZDAV).

## Problem

`node_modules/.vite` accumulates orphaned `deps_temp_<hash>` directories whenever a Vite dep optimisation is interrupted or collides — at intake there were 98 (141 MB), now **95 dirs / 158 MB total in `node_modules/.vite`**. They are pure cache debris: each is a partially written pre-bundle. The epic's AC3 timing work is unaffected functionally, but the debris wastes disk, slows directory scans, and is evidence that dep optimisation is re-running/colliding (which is one source of the transform/import variance measured in AH-0MVF6Y29M005TEOG).

## Why this was not fixed inline

`node_modules` is **shared by every worktree on this host via symlink**; deleting the cache while another agent's suite is mid-run can corrupt that run. The producer rule 'never destroy another agent's work' applies, so the cleanup needs a safe, quiescent mechanism rather than an opportunistic `rm -rf`.

## Expected change

A small, documented, safe cleanup path — e.g. `scripts/clean-vite-cache.mjs` that:
- refuses to run when any `vitest`/`vite` process is alive (or requires `--force`),
- removes only `deps_temp_*` (never the valid `deps/` bundle or `deps_ssr`),
- reports bytes reclaimed, and
- is documented in `docs/dev/test-suite-timing.md` (cache-hygiene section) and optionally wired into `scripts/hygiene_check.sh`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1:** A read-only `--dry-run` (default) reports the orphaned `deps_temp_*` count and bytes; `--apply` removes only those dirs and prints the reclaimed bytes.
- **AC2:** The script refuses to delete while a `vitest`/`vite` process is running unless `--force` is passed, and is covered by tests (dry-run classification, refusal path) that do not require a real cache.
- **AC3:** Documentation states why the cache is shared across worktrees and why the quiescence guard exists.
- **AC4:** After `--apply` on an idle host, `npx vitest run --project unit` still passes (cache regenerates cleanly).

## References

- AH-0MVF6Y29M005TEOG — measured the transform/import cost and rejected the optimizer/isolate/pool variants; notes the collision evidence.
- `scripts/hygiene_check.sh` — the existing periodic hygiene report this could extend.
data.title: Vite dep-cache hygiene: 95 orphaned deps_temp_* dirs (158 MB) in node_modules/.vite

# Align AI_Hell's test framework with the Tableau-Card-Engine game repos

AI_Hell runs a bespoke Vitest setup: `vitest.config.ts` + `vitest.projects.ts` with a
static classifier (`classifyTestFiles` / `isIntegrationTest` in `vitest.projects.ts`)
splitting test files into `unit` / `integration` projects, and test roots `src/`,
`scripts/`, `vite/` — there is **no top-level `tests/` directory**. Every sibling TCE
game repo (and the scaffold template `core/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts`) uses the
standard layout: a `unit` project in `vite.config.ts` with
`include: ['tests/**/*.test.ts']` and no per-file classifier.

**Goal:** bring AI_Hell's test layout and project selection into line with the sibling
repos so cross-repo conventions, agent/audit tooling expectations (top-level `tests/`
tree), and the test skill's type profiles apply uniformly.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **No test lost or doubled.** After migration, AI_Hell's full suite runs the
   identical set of `*.test.ts` files currently selected by
   `vitest.projects.ts::allTestFiles` (src/, scripts/, vite/) — same count and same
   per-file project membership; verified by a before/after selection diff.
2. **Standard layout adopted.** Tests live under a top-level `tests/` tree laid out to
   match sibling repos (e.g. `tests/deploy/` for infra guards, `tests/<area>/`),
   selected via the standard include globs in `vitest.config.ts` (or the config file's
   `test.projects`), with `tsconfig.json` including `tests/**/*.ts`.
3. **Isolation preserved.** Phaser/DOM-booting tests retain their separation from the
   fast node `unit` project (the deliberate unit/integration split — parent
   AH-0MVF3BESP005ZDAV, blocked child AH-0MVF6XV87001NSEJ). Alignment must NOT flatten
   Phaser-heavy tests into the node unit project or regress suite runtime. The
   `src/test/projectMembership.test.ts` guard is updated to assert the new layout and
   still passes.
4. **Tooling keeps working.** The test skill's per-type profiles
   (`.pi/skills_extensions/test/extension.json`, `.pi/test-config.json`) remain
   functional — update only if project names/commands change, and verify each type
   (`unit`, `coverage`, `e2e`) runs.
5. **Documentation updated.** Comments in the vitest config(s), AGENTS.md and any
   dev notes reflect the new layout. CHANGELOG.md excluded (ship skill).
6. **Full suite passes** with the changes.

## Constraints

- Refactor only — no change to app behaviour.
- Preserve the deterministic membership guard pattern (`vitest.projects.ts` is
  deliberately the single source of truth for selection; keep an equivalent guard).
- This item may also relocate `vite/viteWatchIgnore.test.ts` (added by the watch-ignore
  port, MS-0MVBEQ6MC004WRI0) into `tests/deploy/` for full parity — sequence after or
  alongside that port.

## Related work

- MS-0MVBEQ6MC004WRI0 — Port Vite watcher-ignore to sibling game repos (discovering item; adds `vite/viteWatchIgnore.test.ts` under the current layout)
- AH-0MVF3BESP005ZDAV — parent of the unit/integration split decision
- AH-0MVF6XV87001NSEJ — Unit/integration Vitest project split (blocked)
- AH-0MV53ABBU008FKE0 — Test-skill runner no-ops: no .pi/test-config.json suiteCommands for vitest (completed)
data.title: Align AI_Hell test framework with sibling Tableau-Card-Engine game repos (top-level tests/ layout)

# Intake Brief: Promo video scenarios (10+)

**Priority:** medium · **Issue type:** feature · **Assignee:** Map
**Status:** CONFIRMED — producer answered Q1 (b), Q2 (c), Q3 (a) on AH-0MVI5XI73000ZVYA.

## Problem statement

The game can record bot-flown gameplay clips (`npm run capture`) and compile
them into a promo, showreel and highlights (`compile-promo`), and the footage
can only show what the current run happens to contain. Today the only dev
scenarios are capture shortcuts (`boss`, `boss-four-hits`, `defeat`) that jump
to an already-terminal boss fight; there is no curated set of scenes that
showcases the game's range. A promo video therefore needs dedicated,
reproducible scenarios — each pairing an interesting ship configuration with a
deliberate enemy wave — that the Watch Demo and the capture tooling can drive
on demand.

## Users

- **Producer / marketing** — wants a selection of visually distinct, reliably
  capturable moments to assemble into a promo video without hand-playing runs.
- **Player of Watch Demo** — sees varied, interesting bot-flown gameplay in the
  attract loop rather than the same default run each time.

### Example user stories

- As a producer, I want to record a boss battle, a pick-up frenzy and a dense
  enemy horde from fixed, reproducible scenarios so the promo covers each
  editorial category.
- As a player, I want the Watch Demo to fly a variety of bot/loadout and enemy
  combinations so the attract loop shows off the game's range.

## Acceptance criteria

- **AC1 (ten scenarios):** At least 10 scenarios are registered in the shared
  registry (`scripts/capture-scenarios.mjs`) and resolvable via the existing
  `scenario` URL query parameter, dev-gated behind `import.meta.env.DEV`
  exactly like today's scenarios — a production build and a normal run are
  unchanged.
- **AC2 (composition):** Every scenario starts from (i) the **single shipped
  ship config** paired with a **curated bot-tuning preset** in `src/data/
  bot-tuning.json` (optionally a starting weapon/loadout where existing
  mechanics support it) and (ii) a **hand-authored promo wave definition**
  composed from the existing spawner/movement machinery; each scenario is
  deterministic for a given seed and **bot-pilotable end to end**, sustaining
  enough watchable footage for a promo cut (target ≥45 s of action before the
  demo game-over dwell).
- **AC3 (range):** The scenario set evidences every promo editorial category
  from `EDITORIAL_CONFIG` (`weapons`, `pickups`, `enemies`, `boss`) with at
  least one scenario each, and the set is ordered to open with a high
  action-intensity hook so the first captured cut has no dead air.
- **AC4 (capture integration):** `npm run capture -- --list-scenarios` lists
  every scenario with its one-line effect, and `npm run capture --
  --all-scenarios` records one clean clip per scenario.
- **AC5 (tests):** Hermetic tests pin registry ↔ resolver parity, each
  scenario's bot-tuning preset and wave definition, and dev-only gating; an
  integration/demo check confirms a scenario is flown by the Watch Demo bot.
- **AC6 (docs):** All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes,
  including code comments, README, capture `--help` and
  `docs/dev/gameplay-capture.md`.
- **AC7 (suite):** The full project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Scenarios are **dev-only**: gated behind `import.meta.env.DEV` exactly like
  today's scenarios (`src/core/devScenario.ts`); the shipped bundle stays
  inert.
- Single source of truth remains `scripts/capture-scenarios.mjs`; the game
  resolver and the capture CLI must not drift (registry ↔ resolver parity
  test enforced).
- Scenarios are **bot-flown** (the Watch Demo bot / competent bot), reproducible
  per seed, and must not require a human pilot to produce good footage.
- **Wave definitions are new hand-authored content**, but must be composed from
  the **existing spawner/movement machinery** (V/diver swarm, centipede, ghost,
  harvester, horde, strike, lane traffic, asteroid, boss/minion classes) — no
  new gameplay behaviour, so the gym↔game parity and duplicate-body guards in
  `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` are not triggered.
- The shipped ship config (`ship-config.csv`) is **unchanged**; variety comes
  from bot-tuning presets and loadouts, not new ship rows.

## Existing state

- Ship configs: **one** row in `src/data/ship-config.csv` (asteroids scheme,
  thrust 300 px/s², maxSpeed 175 px/s). ShipConfig shape: `configTypes.ts:372`.
- Bot tuning: named presets via `src/core/botTuningStore.ts`, persisted in
  `src/data/bot-tuning.json` (currently one `Default` preset with `competent`
  + `human` layers); Watch Demo flies the current preset
  (AH-0MV6MFDYG001E6PL).
- Waves: static `LEVELS` (`src/waves/Formations.ts`), data-driven difficulty
  curves (`src/data/difficulty-curves.csv`) sequenced by
  `src/waves/sequencedLevels.ts`; spawners per movement class in `src/waves/`.
- Power-ups/weapons: 16 power-up ids and 12 weapon drop ids
  (`src/powerups/types.ts`).
- Scenario infra: registry `scripts/capture-scenarios.mjs` (3 entries),
  resolver `src/core/devScenario.ts`, capture CLI `--scenario /
  --list-scenarios / --all-scenarios`, page-side handle
  `window.__aiHellScenario` to release frozen runs.

## Desired change

Extend the dev-scenario registry so each entry carries the **bot-tuning preset
name** (and optional start loadout) plus its **hand-authored wave definition**
and optional seed. A new promo-wave module (`src/waves/promoScenarios.*`
naming TBD at implementation) hosts the hand-authored definitions, each built
from the existing spawner classes; the scenario resolver applies them at run
start through the existing seams (ship config loading, bot-tuning application,
wave sequencing, run seeding) rather than adding new gameplay. The result is a
catalogue of ≥10 named, documented promo scenarios driveable by
`npm run capture -- --scenario <name>` and the Watch Demo, covering all four
editorial categories and ordered to open with a high-intensity hook.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `scripts/capture-scenarios.mjs` — extend registry entries with bot-tuning
  preset + wave definition + optional loadout/seed metadata.
- `scripts/capture-scenarios.d.mts` — types for the richer entries.
- `src/core/devScenario.ts` — resolve and apply the preset and wave at run
  start; extend the resolved-scenario union.
- `src/core/botTuningStore.ts` / `src/data/bot-tuning.json` — curated presets
  per scenario (Q1 answer: single ship, varied presets).
- `src/waves/` — new hand-authored promo wave definitions reusing existing
  spawner/movement classes, with tests (Q2 answer).
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — scenario application seam at run start.
- `docs/dev/gameplay-capture.md`, `--help`, README — documentation (AC6).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** scenarios are surfaced via the existing registry/URL-param
  pattern plus the capture CLI — no new menu picker unless requested (scope
  creep risk if a visible picker is added later; record as a separate item).
- **Assumption (Q1):** "interesting ship configuration" is delivered through
  bot-tuning/loadout variety on the single shipped ship — no new ShipConfig
  rows. Loadout variety limited to what existing mechanics support.
- **Assumption (Q2):** hand-authored waves live in a new dev-gated module
  composed from existing spawners — content, not new behaviour.
- **Risk:** hand-authored waves must be calibrated so the competent bot
  survives and keeps collecting — a scenario the bot dies in instantly is a
  wasted clip; the ≥45 s sustained-footage target implies some scenarios span
  several waves with the demo game-over dwell only at the end.
- **Risk:** promo footage reads as repetitive if the wave set is a flat list of
  similar archetypes — AC3's category mapping and an intense opening mitigate.
- **Scope-creep risk:** an attract-mode playlist / menu picker for these
  scenarios is out of scope for this item; create a linked follow-up if wanted.

## Related work

- AH-0MV6JGE9R005YOL1 Shared scenario registry and contract tests (completed)
- AH-0MUZM8ATZ002AKFP Batch scenario listing and multi-video capture (completed)
- AH-0MV6JGQFK007MXGX Add --all-scenarios batch capture (completed)
- AH-0MVDV4RJ300459ZF Editorial config and feature-coverage manifest (completed)
- AH-0MVDV4OKN001OT18 Implement: pure edit-plan and selection logic in compile-promo (completed)
- AH-0MVDV50Z20071RF4 Produce and validate the promo, showreel and highlight clips (completed)
- AH-0MV6MFDYG001E6PL Watch Demo and video recording should fly the saved bot-tuning configuration (completed)
- AH-0MV29SBAQ000HQR2 Add 5 new levels before the boss showcasing the classic-arcade enemy roster (completed)

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "Ship configurations: only one ShipConfig exists today. Where should the
  'interesting ship configuration' per scenario come from? (a) Author 2–4
  additional ShipConfig rows; (b) Keep the single ship; vary the
  bot-tuning/loadout preset instead; (c) Both." —
  **Answer (producer): (b) Keep the single ship; vary the bot-tuning/loadout
  preset instead.** Source: interactive reply on the work item, 2026-10-27.
  Research: `src/data/ship-config.csv` has one row; `botTuningStore` supports
  named presets (`bot-tuning.json`); Watch Demo already flies the current
  preset. Final ACs reflect preset/loadout variety, no new ship rows.
- Q2: "Enemy waves: where do the waves come from? (a) Reuse existing campaign
  content plus a few hand-authored waves; (b) Reuse existing content only;
  (c) Hand-author all new promo-tailored wave definitions." —
  **Answer (producer): (c) Hand-author all new promo-tailored wave
  definitions.** Source: interactive reply on the work item, 2026-10-27.
  Research: spawner/movement classes exist per archetype in `src/waves/`;
  hand-authored definitions reuse them, keeping the parity guards quiet.
- Q3: "'Wide range of experiences': how should the 10+ scenarios be defined?
  (a) Map across the promo editorial categories (weapons, pickups, enemies,
  boss), open with a high-intensity hook; (b) Showcase specific enemy
  archetypes without category mapping; (c) Simplest 10+ slots." —
  **Answer (producer): (a) Map across editorial categories; open with a high
  action-intensity hook.** Source: interactive reply on the work item,
  2026-10-27. Research: `EDITORIAL_CONFIG.categories` in
  `scripts/compile-promo.mjs`; the coverage manifest requires every category
  to be evidenced.
data.title: Create a number of scenarios that will be useful in creating a promo video

## Goal

Crash resilience for dev telemetry: with the dev JSONL sink moving to an in-memory per-run buffer (AH-0MVIRYGD1000JVY3), a page reload or crash mid-run loses the un-uploaded tail. Streaming telemetry batches to the dev server during the run — instead of one run-end upload — bounds that loss to at most one flushed batch (~64 records, ~1.3 s of play) and removes the page-reload regression that localStorage previously masked.

## Context

- Parent/related: discovered-from:AH-0MVIRYGD1000JVY3 (in-memory dev sink; this item is explicitly deferred there).
- Current flow: the JsonlTelemetrySink buffers records in memory, flushes batches of 64 to the sink, and the whole run is POSTed once at run end (`uploadDevTelemetry`). A crash before that POST loses the entire run's telemetry; a reload also loses the buffer entirely once it is no longer localStorage-backed.
- Dev only: the same reasoning applies to the production remote sink, which already streams batches via `HttpTelemetryTransport` (with retry/backoff), so production is not affected.

## Proposed design

- Send each flushed batch to the dev endpoint as it is produced (`POST /api/telemetry/upload`) instead of (or in addition to) the run-end upload.
- The server (`vite/plugins/telemetryUploadPlugin.ts`) currently stores each upload as one complete `session-<stamp>.jsonl` and runs the automatic evaluation per upload; a per-batch POST would create many tiny recordings and repeated evaluations. The endpoint (or a new `part` protocol) must therefore either:
  - append JSONL records to the run's open session file keyed by a run id/seed, and evaluate once at run end, or
  - keep the run-end upload and add a lightweight "heartbeat/checkpoint" mechanism that only recovers the tail on demand.
- UX/offline: batches sent while the dev server is unreachable should stay in the memory buffer (or a bounded queue) and be retried at run end; at most one batch may be lost on a hard crash.

## Acceptance criteria

- AC1: A mid-run crash/reload followed by a run-end state loses no more than one flushed batch (~64 records / ~1.3 s) of telemetry; the rest is recoverable from the dev server.
- AC2: The server session file for a run contains its records exactly once (no duplication from partial + final uploads), and the automatic evaluation still runs once per run.
- AC3: Dev CLI tooling (`record-session`, `capture-gameplay`, `verify-dev-telemetry`) continues to work unchanged in behaviour.
- AC4: Full project test suite passes.

## Status

Open decision item — parked until the in-memory sink (AH-0MVIRYGD1000JVY3) lands. Do not implement concurrently with that item in the same worktree.
data.title: Crash resilience: incremental telemetry upload so a mid-run reload loses at most one batch

# Implement the Music System defined by the Audio Design Chapter

## Goal

Build the runtime background-music system for AI Hell against the fixed design contract captured in
`docs/AUDIO_DESIGN_CHAPTER.md` (produced by **Update GDD with Audio Design Chapter (AH-0MVAUUV1U005UM4W)**).

User story: *As a player, I want a dynamic, retro-arcade soundtrack that responds to combat intensity, so
that runs feel like the relentless survival experience the game is aiming for; and as a developer I want the
music engine driven by a documented parameter/state contract, so behaviour is testable and reproducible.*

> **Scope stance:** this is **future scope, out of MVP** (GDD §8). The MVP ships baked ToneForge SFX only
> (GDD §7.3), and §7.3 remains authoritative for SFX. This item must **not** be started until the design
> chapter exists and has been reviewed, and it must **not** promote music into the MVP without an explicit
> producer decision.

## Background

- AI Hell currently has **no background music** by design: GDD §7.3 keeps music out of MVP scope, and the
  player-fire grid is deliberately quantised to a **silent internal 80 BPM beat** (AH-0MUAYB8EH005RJ8B).
- SFX are build-time baked WAV assets rendered deterministically by ToneForge and played through Phaser's
  shared `AudioContext` (`src/audio/effects.ts`); the authoritative cue catalogue is
  `docs/AUDIO_TONEFORGE_CUE_MAPPING.md`.
- The Audio Design Chapter specifies the musical identity (Phrygian Dominant combat scale, Lydian ambient
  scale, Combat Motifs A/B, "Star Drift"), instrumentation palette, dynamic-mixing rules, state-driven
  transitions, parameter mapping, audio budget and accessibility requirements.

## Expected behaviour and outcomes

- A music system that plays layered/stemmed music driven by an explicit game-state parameter, with
  bar-boundary transitions, stingers, and ducking, as specified by the chapter.
- Music state follows gameplay (e.g. menu/attract, wave combat, boss, low-health tension, run end) with the
  transition rules and timings given in the chapter, and never disrupts the beat grid or the SFX mix.
- Reproducible, deterministic behaviour suitable for automated tests; no audio regressions to the shipped SFX
  pipeline.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — Contract traceable to the chapter:** every implemented music state, transition, stinger and mixing parameter traces to a named section of `docs/AUDIO_DESIGN_CHAPTER.md`, recorded in a mapping table in the implementation docs.
- [ ] **AC2 — Musical content matches the documented identity:** the delivered cues/stems use the chapter's scales, motifs and progressions (Phrygian Dominant combat, Lydian ambient, Combat Motifs A/B, "Star Drift"), verified by an explicit audit table (motif → scale degrees → usage state).
- [ ] **AC3 — State machine implemented and tested:** transitions occur only at the documented boundaries (bar boundaries unless a stinger cut-in is specified), with unit tests covering each transition in the chapter's transition matrix, including invalid/reset paths.
- [ ] **AC4 — Dynamic mixing implemented:** ducking, per-layer volume targets and the priority tiers behave as specified; SFX intelligibility is preserved (music ducks under key SFX cues) and is covered by tests.
- [ ] **AC5 — Autoplay and accessibility compliance:** no audio before a user gesture (`AudioContext` resume discipline, GDD §7.3); the chapter's accessibility requirements (e.g. music/SFX independent volume, mute, and any reduction options) are implemented and documented.
- [ ] **AC6 — Budget met:** the shipped music respects the chapter's audio budget (memory, streaming, polyphony, layer count) on the supported targets, measured and recorded.
- [ ] **AC7 — Docs updated:** GDD §7.3 and §8 are updated to reflect the shipped music system, and `docs/AUDIO_DESIGN_CHAPTER.md` is marked as implemented for the sections that ship.
- [ ] **AC8 — No SFX regression:** the existing ToneForge baked-SFX pipeline and cue catalogue remain unchanged and their tests pass; any chapter §6.4 procedural SFX recipes are explicitly **not** adopted unless decisioned separately.
- [ ] **AC9 — Full project build and test suite pass.**

## Constraints

- **Blocked by** the docs item **Update GDD with Audio Design Chapter (AH-0MVAUUV1U005UM4W)** — this item
  must not begin before `docs/AUDIO_DESIGN_CHAPTER.md` exists.
- Music stays **out of MVP scope** until a producer decision promotes it (GDD §7.3, §8).
- Keep the gameplay SVG/vector aesthetic and retro-arcade palette of the chapter; UK English in all docs.
- §7.3 (baked ToneForge SFX) remains authoritative for SFX; the chapter is an addendum whose §6.4 procedural
  SFX recipes are design reference only.
- Prefer reusing the existing audio plumbing (`src/audio/effects.ts`, shared `AudioContext`, manifest-driven
  playback) over introducing new runtime dependencies; any middleware adoption (the chapter's FMOD/Wwise
  guidance) is a separate decision — the web build currently has no middleware.

## Approach (indicative)

1. Confirm scope with the producer (MVP vs post-MVP) and record the decision on this item.
2. Ingest the chapter into an implementation mapping table (state → parameter → cue/stem set → transition).
3. Decide the delivery mechanism (baked stems via ToneForge + `AudioContext` playback, per the existing
   pipeline) versus a runtime synthesiser; record the trade-off before coding.
4. Implement the music state machine and mixing layer behind a single facade, mirroring the existing SFX
   façade style; add unit tests per transition and per mixing rule.
5. Add accessibility controls and the autoplay guard; verify budget and measure on target hardware.
6. Update GDD §7.3/§8 and the chapter's implemented-sections marker.

**Key Files:**
- `docs/AUDIO_DESIGN_CHAPTER.md` — the design contract (prerequisite)
- `src/audio/effects.ts` — existing SFX façade / shared `AudioContext` plumbing to reuse
- `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts` — where combat-state music parameters would be driven from
- `src/core/rules.ts` — game-rules config (including `beatBpm`) that music tempo must stay coherent with
- `src/audio/` — new music module + tests
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — §7.3 and §8 updates

## Risks & assumptions

- **Overlap with the shipped silent beat grid (medium):** player fire is quantised to an internal 80 BPM beat.
  Music must be tempo-coherent with that grid or the two will fight; assume music tempo is either locked to
  `beatBpm` or documented as intentionally independent.
- **Chapter/SFX divergence (medium):** the chapter's §6.4 procedural SFX recipes differ from the shipped baked
  catalogue; §7.3 stays authoritative (AC8).
- **Middleware assumption (low):** the chapter's FMOD/Wwise guidance is forward-looking; no middleware exists in
  the web build, so it is design intent only.
- **Scope creep into MVP (medium):** music is out of MVP; promotion needs an explicit producer decision.

## Related work

- **Update GDD with Audio Design Chapter (AH-0MVAUUV1U005UM4W)** — prerequisite; produces the design contract.

- GDD §7.3 (SFX, authoritative for MVP), GDD §8 (Future Scope — "Background music"), and

  explosion accents).

data.description:
# Bot should be aware of screen wrap around (AH-0MVMISF0Q00314LG)

## Problem statement

The game's playfield is a wrap-around (torus) arena — the player ship, asteroids,
bullets and raider patrol all cross a screen edge and reappear on the opposite
side — but the AI bot's decision layer (`src/ai/`) is wrap-blind: it treats the
four bounding edges as solid walls it must not approach, never crosses a seam on
purpose, and measures every distance, bearing, aim solution, threat prediction
and nearest-selection along the raw (unwrapped) straight line. A human player
routinely uses the seam to chase, flee and angle shots; the bot cannot, so demo
play looks unhuman, the bot camps near the walls it wrongly fears, and it
systematically misjudges everything on the far side of an edge.

## Users

- **Players / viewers of the attract demo** — the demo bot is deliberately
  human-like (human reaction cadence, W/A/D controls, thrust feel); humans use
  the wrap, so a bot that refuses to is conspicuous.
- **Developers** — one coherent torus model in the decision layer, so future
  features (seam-aware enemy fire, new archetypes, tuning) share a single
  implementation instead of adding seam hacks.

### Example user stories

- As a **player watching the demo**, I want the bot to cross a screen edge to
  reach a target that is closer the other way, so its movement looks like a
  human's.
- As a **player**, I want the demo bot to aim and fire at an enemy along the
  shortest wrapped path — including off one edge to arrive from the opposite
  edge — so engagements play out in the whole wrap-around arena.
- As a **player**, I want the bot to dodge a shot that is about to arrive
  across the seam, so it survives what any human sees coming.
- As a **developer**, I want one wrap-aware geometry implementation used by
  steering, aim, prediction and distance, so the model is consistent and
  testable, and the headless eval measures the same physics the bot faces in
  the game.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Wrap-aware steering (movement)** — The four arena edges stop being walls in
   the steering safety/clearance test: both the legacy `evaluateVector`
   (`src/ai/botDecision.ts`) and the competent `evaluateDirection`
   (`src/ai/framework/competent/steering.ts`) no longer reject a direction
   solely because it reaches an edge within `wallMargin`, and steering toward an
   objective uses the **shortest wrapped path** (the closer of the raw bearing
   and the seam-crossing bearing to the objective's opposite-edge duplicate) so
   the bot crosses an edge to get to the other side — used deliberately when
   net-positive (Q2), never as a scripted trick. Unit tests cover each of the
   four edges: the wrapped bearing is chosen when it is shorter; an
   edge-crossing direction is safe when it does not otherwise threaten.

2. **Seam-aware aim & targeting** — Aim and target selection run on the torus:
   `bearingTo`/`interceptPoint` and the legacy aim compute deltas along the
   shortest wrapped path, and `nearestTarget` / `nearestEnemyDistance` choose
   nearest by wrapped distance. When the wrapped route to an enemy, boss or
   mineral is shorter than the raw line, the bot points at the seam duplicate —
   firing off one edge to arrive from the opposite edge. Tests assert the aim
   angle equals the wrapped-path angle when that route is shorter, and that
   behaviour is unchanged when the raw line is already shortest.

3. **Seam-aware threat & hazard prediction** — `predictIncomingFire`
   (`worldModel.ts`), the competent `closestApproach` solves and the legacy
   path-crossing checks operate on the wrapped torus, so shots and moving
   hazards whose closest approach to the player crosses a seam are predicted and
   dodged. The `hazardVelocity` tracker's existing wrap-jump clamp is
   re-verified so it does not double-compensate once positions are modelled on
   the torus. Tests: a seam-crossing shot is classified as threatening (a
   raw-line-only view would miss it).

4. **`wallMargin` retired cleanly** — The now-meaningless wall-margin tunable is
   retired (or demonstrably re-purposed) across `botDecision.ts`,
   `competent/tunables.ts`, `style/fitting.ts` and `tuningFields.ts`; saved
   bot-tuning configs (`src/data/bot-tuning.json` and any gym-saved tunings)
   still load with the field gone (unknown-field tolerance), and the style-fit
   mapping is updated per the retirement. Documented in the tuning UI/docs.

5. **Eval parity** — The headless eval arena (`src/ai/eval/arena.ts`) is brought
   to wrap-parity with the game: enemy bullets wrap at the edges instead of
   being culled off-field, and hostile fire aims along the shortest wrapped
   path (matching the seam-aware aim the enemy wrap epic ships), so eval scores
   measure wrap-aware play. `arena.test.ts` covers the wrapped-bullet and
   seam-aim cases.

6. **Testing, validation & docs** — Unit/integration tests cover wrapped steering
   (all four edges, raw vs. wrapped), seam aim, seam threat prediction, wrapped
   nearest-selection when raw and wrapped ordering differ, wall-margin
   retirement and eval parity. The human-like governor's reaction cadence,
   controls and thrust feel are unchanged (existing steering/bot integration
   tests stay green, plus new wrap scenarios). `docs/BOT_FRAMEWORK.md` and
   `docs/EVALUATION.md` are updated to describe the wrap-aware model. The full
   project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Constraints

- One shared implementation in the bot decision layer — no divergent per-behaviour
  seam copies; share/adapt the seam maths the enemy wrap epic develops rather
  than reinventing.
- The human-like governor (`src/ai/botHumanLike.ts`) is preserved: reaction
  cadence, W/A/D + optional reverse, seeded aim-skill noise and human-feel
  thrust presses are unchanged; wrap-awareness is a model property, not a
  scripted manœuvre.
- Use the seam when it is net-positive (Q2) — nearest-wrapped-path selection
  already yields that; no deliberate "wrap tricks".
- Do not change game physics (player/enemy/bullet wrap models); the bot's model
  must match the game, not alter it.
- Written in UK English per repo convention.

## Existing state (evidence)

- **Player wraps at all four edges** — `src/utils/movementModel.ts`
  (`if (x < 0) x += width; if (x >= width) x -= width;` and same for y). The
  headless eval arena drives the bot through the same `asteroidModel.tick(width,
  height)`, so the bot's own ship already wraps there.
- **Bullets wrap (game)** — `src/scenes/core/bulletLifecycle.ts` four-edge wrap;
  raider patrol wraps (`src/scenes/core/raiderPatrol.ts`). **Eval culls bullets
  off-field instead** (`src/ai/eval/arena.ts` `offField`), and hostile fire
  there aims at the raw player position.
- **Bot treats edges as walls** — legacy `botDecision.ts` `evaluateVector`
  ("a direction is unsafe when it reaches a wall within `wallMargin`") and
  competent `steering.ts` `evaluateDirection` (same); both tuned by a
  `wallMargin` knob (`botDecision.ts:189`, `competent/tunables.ts:239`,
  `style/fitting.ts`, `tuningFields.ts:94`).
- **All geometry is raw Euclidean** — `competent/goals.ts` `nearestTarget`
  (`Math.hypot`), `competent/steering.ts` `bearingTo` / `interceptPoint` /
  `closestApproach`, `worldModel.ts` `nearestEnemyDistance` /
  `predictIncomingFire`, `botDecision.ts` distance / closestApproach.
- **Existing wrap compensation, not awareness** — `src/ai/framework/hazardVelocity.ts`
  deliberately clamps spurious position jumps caused by wrap/respawn.
- **Tests assert the bot never wraps** — `botSteering.integration.test.ts`
  ("it never wraps the screen").
- **Enemy wrap epic in flight** — AH-0MV9G3DZ9003P7P8 makes enemies wrap and fire
  across seams (blocked child slices AH-0MVKXBV0O005Q77P, AH-0MVKXBWDY008R0YH,
  AH-0MVKXBSAD003VRMF, AH-0MVKXBTNJ003F1TC, AH-0MVKXBXQX003S7K5,
  AH-0MVKXBZ5N007LKH4); once it lands, a wrap-blind bot fails to aim or dodge
  seam fire at all.

## Desired change

Give the bot's decision layer a single, shared wrap-aware (torus) model:

1. **Wrap-aware steering primitives** in the decision layer — a wrapped bearing /
   delta helper alongside the existing raw geometry, with a small hysteresis at
   nearly-equal raw/wrapped paths so targeting does not flip duplicates every
   tick; use it for the four steering/clearance tests (legacy + competent) and
   for `bearingTo`/`interceptPoint`.
2. **Wrapped nearest-selection** — `nearestTarget`, `nearestEnemyDistance` and
   the collect/engage/evade distances use wrapped distance; evade flees across a
   seam when that is the safest separation.
3. **Seam-aware prediction** — `predictIncomingFire` and the closest-approach
   solves run on the torus; verify `hazardVelocity` still clamps only true
   teleports.
4. **`wallMargin` retirement** — remove/re-purpose the knob and its style-fit
   mapping; keep saved configs loading.
5. **Eval parity** — wrap enemy bullets, aim hostile fire along the shortest
   wrapped path, and update `arena.test.ts` so metrics capture wrap-aware play.
6. **Docs & tests** — update `docs/BOT_FRAMEWORK.md` / `docs/EVALUATION.md`; add
   the wrap-scenario tests from AC1–AC5.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/ai/framework/competent/steering.ts` — wrap-aware `evaluateDirection`
  (no wall-margin wall test), `bearingTo`, `interceptPoint`, `closestApproach`.
- `src/ai/framework/competent/goals.ts` — `nearestTarget` and goal distances on
  the wrapped torus.
- `src/ai/framework/worldModel.ts` — `nearestEnemyDistance`, `predictIncomingFire`
  on the torus.
- `src/ai/framework/competent/behaviours.ts` — collect/engage/evade distances
  and the evade flee direction.
- `src/ai/botDecision.ts` — legacy `evaluateVector`, legacy aim/aim-delta and
  closest-approach paths.
- `src/ai/framework/hazardVelocity.ts` — re-verify the wrap-jump clamp under the
  torus model; adjust only if double-compensating.
- `src/ai/framework/competent/tunables.ts`, `src/ai/botDecision.ts`,
  `src/ai/style/fitting.ts`, `src/ai/tuningFields.ts`,
  `src/data/bot-tuning.json` — retire/re-purpose `wallMargin`; keep config
  loading tolerant.
- `src/ai/eval/arena.ts` + `arena.test.ts` — wrapped enemy bullets, seam-aware
  hostile aim, parity tests.
- `docs/BOT_FRAMEWORK.md`, `docs/EVALUATION.md` — describe the wrap-aware model.
- Tests: `src/ai/framework/competent/steering.test.ts`,
  `src/ai/framework/worldModel.test.ts`, `src/ai/botDecision.test.ts`,
  `src/ai/botSteering.integration.test.ts`,
  `src/ai/framework/competent/competentBot.integration.test.ts`, plus a
  dedicated wrap-geometry unit test module.

## Related work

- **AH-0MV9G3DZ9003P7P8** — "Enemies should be aware of the wrap around" (open
  epic with blocked child slices). Enemy counterpart: wrap-aware enemy movement
  and seam-aware enemy fire. Directly relevant — share the seam maths/helpers
  and sequence work so the bot and enemies land coherently.
- **AH-0MU960UTE001PTV0** — "Bullets should have a distance and should wrap
  around the screen" (completed) — the wrap model the game's bullets use.
- **AH-0MUY08WX3000ZEVO** — "Structured competent bot: utility goals, behaviour
  tree, predictive dodge/aim" (completed) — the competent layer this change
  extends.
- **AH-0MUXXQ1MN002RXGB** — "Demo bot: human-like input limits" (completed) —
  the human-like governor whose look-and-feel must be preserved.
- **AH-0MVI4QDN90037DIN** — "Predict enemy movement (bot)" (completed) — the
  hazard-velocity tracker whose wrap clamp interacts with the torus model.
- **AH-0MVP5IGX5005XTVV** — "Bot tuning scene is not using the same gameplay
  objects as the main game" (open) — bot/gym parity concern; watch for overlap.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk: duplicate flapping** — when the raw path and the wrapped path are
  nearly equal, a naive min-distance choice can flip between two seam
  duplicates every tick; mitigated with a small hysteresis/tolerance at near-equal
  lengths (the commitment layer already adds some hysteresis).
- **Risk: `wallMargin` migration ripple** — the knob appears across tunables,
  style-fitting, the tuning UI and saved `bot-tuning.json`; handle removal so
  saved configs keep loading, update the fit mapping, and document the behaviour
  change for old configs.
- **Risk: double-compensation** — `hazardVelocity` clamps wrap jumps today;
  once positions are modelled on the torus, verify the tracker only clamps true
  teleports/respawns and never swallows legitimate seam re-entry.
- **Risk: eval divergence** — the headless arena must mirror the game's wrap
  physics or wrap-aware behaviour earns no eval credit; keep the parity change
  minimal (bullet wrap + seam aim) and covered by `arena.test.ts`.
- **Scope-creep guard** — out of scope: game physics changes, non-torus
  pathfinding/routing, scripted wrap manœuvres, and any enemy/wrap changes
  beyond the arena-parity bump. Anything extra found becomes a linked work item,
  not silent scope growth.
- **Assumption: dimensions** — the bot already receives playfield dimensions via
  tunables (`playfieldWidth`/`playfieldHeight`, 960×540), so the torus needs no
  snapshot changes.
- **Assumption: seam maths reuse** — the enemy wrap epic (AH-0MV9G3DZ9003P7P8)
  will have developed wrapped-delta helpers; reuse/adapt rather than duplicate.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "Scope of wrap-awareness for the bot? (a) Movement/steering only. (b) +
  seam-aware aim/targeting. (c) Full torus model — plus seam-aware threat/hazard
  prediction." — Answer (Map): "(c) Full torus model". Source: producer reply on
  the work item (comment thread AH-C0MVR682R00022NOC). Research: steering walls
  in `botDecision.ts` + `steering.ts`, raw Euclidean geometry throughout
  (`goals.ts`, `worldModel.ts`, `behaviours.ts`), enemy wrap epic
  AH-0MV9G3DZ9003P7P8 in flight.
- Q2: "Should the bot deliberately *use* the seam as a manœuvre, or merely stop
  avoiding edges?" — Answer (Map): "Use it when net-positive". Source: producer
  reply on the work item. Research: nearest-wrapped-path selection yields
  net-positive seam use naturally; no scripted trick, human-like governor
  unchanged.
- Q3: "Should the headless eval arena be brought to wrap-parity with the game so
  eval measures wrap-aware play?" — Answer (Map): "Yes". Source: producer reply
  on the work item. Research: `arena.ts` culls enemy bullets off-field and aims
  hostile fire at the raw player position — both diverge from the game.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MU960UTE001PTV0** – Bullets should have a distance and should wrap around the screen (completed)
- **AH-0MV9G3DZ9003P7P8** – Enemies should be aware of the wrap around (open)
- **AH-0MU8FOQ7L005AII0** – Core Asteroid Entity + Unit Tests (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `README.md` — matched: around, aware, bot, currently, edge, get, off, one, screen, should, side, wrap
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — matched: around, aware, bot, currently, edge, get, off, one, screen, should, side, wrap
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: around, aware, bot, currently, edge, get, off, one, screen, should, side, wrap

## Context

The producer decided (2026-10-27) that AI Hell will NOT run the full test suite in the pre-push hook — the suite runs repeatedly during implementation via the test skill (`/skill:test`, `run_tests.py`). The committed `.githooks/pre-push` keeps its v2 behaviour (branch policy, context budget, `wl sync`); the item AH-0MVMA87GX0061KUQ was re-purposed as a decision record and closed.

## Future conflict to revisit

SorraAgents **SA-0MVNUMMOA002LCB1** (open) plans to make the framework v3 pre-push hook resolve `run_tests.py` local-then-global and ship v3 to every project via `scripts/install_pi.sh`, with an upgrade path that replaces installed hooks carrying an old unmodified framework revision marker (backup + report). AI Hell's current `.githooks/pre-push` is an unmodified framework v2 copy, so when that lands, `install_pi.sh` would likely replace it with the gated v3 hook — silently re-introducing a full-suite gate and reversing the decision.

## Desired change

When SA-0MVNUMMOA002LCB1 lands (or during its review), choose how to preserve the no-gate decision:

- (a) keep the hook locally modified (a deliberate deviation that `install_pi.sh` reports rather than overwrites);
- (b) default `TEST_SCOPE_SKIP=1` in the installed hook;
- (c) accept the gate (reversing the decision).

Record the choice on this item and update any local documentation.

## Acceptance criteria

- When SA-0MVNUMMOA002LCB1's v3 hook / installer upgrade reaches AI Hell (or is reviewed as an SA item), this item's decision is actioned and the outcome recorded here.
- AI Hell's `.githooks/pre-push` does not silently gain a full-suite gate without an explicit producer decision.
- A comment on this item links the relevant SA commit/PR and states the chosen option.

# Intake brief — Weapon upgrades are too powerful

> Operator seed intent: "All weapons, except the starting weapon, are too
> powerful at lvl 0 and their upgrades are too rapid. Scale everything back a
> little."
>
> Producer decisions (recorded 2026-10-30, see Appendix): **Q1 = A with a 40 %
> trim**, **Q2 = A and it applies to every weapon including the cannon's
> upgrade levels**, **Q3 = B** (numeric budgets **plus** a measured batch gate).
> Level-0 cannon values stay untouched.

## Problem statement

Every weapon except the starting cannon is stronger than it should be at
**level 0**, and the *step* each upgrade adds is so large that a mid-run build
trivialises waves: the first weapon level of any single-shot weapon roughly
**triples** its bullet count (`projectileCount` level 1 = **+2** extra
projectiles), and fire rate then compounds on top. The operator wants the whole
non-cannon catalogue scaled back by **40 % of its level-0 output**, the
per-level curve **flattened for every weapon including the cannon's own
levels**, and the result **measured** against the existing batch-evaluation
harness.

## Users

- **Player** — wants weapon pickups to feel like a modest, earned advantage so
  waves stay tense instead of becoming a screen-clear once a build forms.
  - *As a player, I want picking up a second or third weapon to make the fight
    easier but not automatic, so I still have to fly well.*
- **Designer / balancing agent** — needs the weapon strength budget expressed
  as inspectable, committed numbers so "40 %" and "flatter" can be tested and a
  future weapon checked against the same budget.
  - *As a designer, I want a level-0 output table and a per-level growth ceiling
    stored beside the data, so balance intent cannot drift from the values.*
- **Agent / gym user** — the game and every gym must keep running the identical
  catalogue and resolver (gym↔game parity), so the nerf is a data change, never
  a divergent code path.

## Evidence gathered (current behaviour, measured from the code)

Level 0 single-target output, derived from `DEFAULT_WEAPON_SUBDIVISIONS`
(80 BPM beat grid → 1.333 beats/s) × pattern count × hit budget, relative to the
cannon. **This table is the baseline the 40 % trim is measured against and is to
be committed as a test fixture / GDD table.**

| Weapon | Pattern at L0 | Shots/s | Effective hits/s (single target) | × cannon |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| cannon (unchanged at L0) | 1 bullet | 2.67 | 2.67 | 1.00× |
| spread | 3-bullet fan ±30° | 1.33 | 4.00 | 1.50× |
| dual | 2 parallel bullets | 1.33 | 2.67 | 1.00× |
| rapid | 1 bullet, 6/beat | 8.00 | 8.00 | **3.00×** |
| wave_laser | 1 beam, 2 HP budget | 1.33 | 2.67 (5.33 across two targets) | 2.00× |
| ricochet | 1 pellet, 2 wall bounces | 1.33 | 4.00 (up to 3 targets) | 1.50× |
| cluster | missile + 2 warheads | 0.67 | 2.00 radial | 0.75× |
| options | 2 orbiting pods, radial | 1.33 | 2.67 all-round | 1.00× |
| nova | AoE ring, 45 px | 0.33 | every enemy in 45 px | role-defined |
| mortar | AoE, 35 px, random point | 0.67 | every enemy in 35 px | role-defined |
| arc | AoE + chain, 60 px | 1.33 | chained targets in 60 px | role-defined |
| rear_guard | 1 backward bullet | 2.67 | 2.67 (rear arc) | 1.00× |
| broadside | 2 perpendicular bullets | 0.67 | 1.33 | 0.50× |
| railgun | 1 tracer, 5 HP budget | 0.33 | 1.67 (5 across targets) | 0.63× |
| shard_swarm | 5-shard fan ±15° | 1.33 | 6.67 | **2.50×** |
| heavy_slug | 1 oversized slug | 0.67 | 0.67 (larger hit area) | 0.25× |

Weapons are **cumulative**, so a run's total output is the sum of every active
weapon plus the cannon — a single pick is not the unit of power.

Per-level growth, worked through `resolveWeaponAtLevel` for a single-shot
weapon (cannon pattern, quantised to the beat grid). **This is the baseline the
curve flattening is measured against.**

| Level | Extra projectiles (bullet count) | Fire-rate multiplier (quantised) | Effective hits/s | × level 0 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | 0 (1) | 1.00 (375 ms) | 2.67 | 1.0× |
| 1 | **2 (3)** | 1.33 (250 ms) | 12.00 | **4.5×** |
| 2 | 3 (4) | 1.60 (250 ms) | 16.00 | 6.0× |
| 3 | 4 (5) | 1.83 (187.5 ms) | 26.67 | 10.0× |
| 4 | 5 (6) | 2.03 (187.5 ms) | 32.00 | 12.0× |
| 5 | 5 (6) | 2.19 (187.5 ms) | 32.00 | 12.0× |

So the complaint resolves to two independent, measurable causes:

1. **Level-0 baselines are uneven** — rapid is 3× the cannon, shard_swarm 2.5×,
   spread/ricochet 1.5×, and the pierce weapons double their output whenever a
   second enemy lines up.
2. **The first levels jump, they do not ramp** — `projectileCount`'s first step
   is **+2 bullets** (k = 0.22 over a cap of 8), which triples every
   single-projectile weapon at level 1; fire rate then compounds on top.

## Desired change (decided)

### 1. Level-0 trim of every non-cannon weapon (Q1 = A, 40 %)

- Every non-cannon weapon's level-0 **output is cut by 40 %** (i.e. to **60 %
  of its baseline in the table above**), so the run's total output grows far
  more slowly as weapons stack.
- The **~1.5× cannon single-target ceiling takes precedence** where 60 % is not
  enough: today rapid is 3.0× (60 % = 1.8×, still over) and shard_swarm 2.5×
  (60 % = 1.5×, exactly at the cap), so rapid is trimmed further to 1.5×.
- **Weapon identity is preserved**: prefer slowing the on-beat cadence over
  deleting a pattern bullet or a pierce budget that *is* the weapon's identity.
  The measure of "output" per family: single-target **hits/s** for projectile
  weapons, **pierce/bounce depth × hits/s** for budget weapons, **coverage area
  × cadence** for the AOE family (nova/mortar/arc), and **pod count × cadence**
  for Options.
- **On-grid realisation**: fire rates must stay exact beat subdivisions
  (`isOnBeatGrid`), and pattern/budget counts are integers, so where an exact
  60 % is not representable the nearest on-grid value **at or below** the
  target (60 % or lower) is used and the realised percentage is recorded.
- The **cannon's level-0 values are unchanged**.

Proposed realisation (the plan may refine the lever per weapon, but must stay
inside the bound; AoE radius uses `radius × 0.775` ≈ 60 % area):

| Weapon | Baseline hits/s | Lever | Proposed | % of baseline |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| spread | 4.00 | cadence 1/beat → 0.5/beat | 2.00 | 50 % |
| dual | 2.67 | cadence 1/beat → 0.5/beat | 1.33 | 50 % |
| rapid | 8.00 | cadence 6/beat → 3/beat (1.5× cap binds) | 4.00 | 50 % |
| wave_laser | 2.67 (2 targets 5.33) | cadence 1/beat → 0.5/beat, budget 2 kept | 1.33 (2.67) | 50 % |
| ricochet | 4.00 | cadence 1/beat → 0.5/beat, bounce 2 kept | 2.00 | 50 % |
| cluster | 2.00 | cadence 0.5/beat → 0.25/beat | 1.00 | 50 % |
| options | 2.67 | cadence 1/beat → 0.5/beat, 2 pods kept | 1.33 | 50 % |
| nova | 45 px ring | radius 45 → 35 px (60 % area) | — | 60 % |
| mortar | 35 px blast | radius 35 → 27 px | — | 60 % |
| arc | 60 px chain | radius 60 → 46 px | — | 60 % |
| rear_guard | 2.67 | cadence 2/beat → 1/beat | 1.33 | 50 % |
| broadside | 1.33 | cadence 0.5/beat → 0.25/beat | 0.67 | 50 % |
| railgun | 1.67 (5 targets 8.33) | HP budget 5 → 3 (cadence is already 3 s) | 1.00 | 60 % |
| shard_swarm | 6.67 | 5 shards → 3 shards at 1/beat | 4.00 | 60 % (1.5× cap) |
| heavy_slug | 0.67 | cadence 0.5/beat → 0.25/beat | 0.33 | 50 % |

### 2. Flatten the per-level curve — all weapons, including the cannon's levels (Q2 = A)

- `projectileCount` — base 0, **cap 8 → 4**, **k 0.22 → ~0.18**, so **level 1
  adds +1 projectile, not +2** (the current +2 is the dominant spike). The level
  cap becomes +4 extra projectiles (5 for a single-shot pattern) instead of +8.
- `fireRate` — **cap 3 → ~2.2**, **k 0.18 → ~0.12**, so the first level is a
  ≈1.1–1.15× multiplier that mostly quantises to *no* extra beat step for a
  2/beat weapon, and the ceiling is ≈2.2× instead of 3×.
- `bulletSize` — cap 2.5 → ~2.0, k 0.16 → ~0.12 (hit probability grows more
  slowly).
- `aoeRadius` — cap 2.5 → ~2.0, k 0.18 → ~0.12 (AOE coverage grows more slowly).
- **Targets**: level-1 resolved output **≤ 2.5× level 0** (today 4.5×), and
  level-cap (saturated) output **≤ 50 % of today's level-cap output**
  (today ~27× level 0 for the cannon pattern, so ≤ ~13.5×).
- The retuned specs apply to **every** weapon's levels, including the cannon's;
  only the cannon's **level-0** values are frozen.
- The `rationale` string beside each spec is rewritten so the intent stays
  beside the numbers (the existing convention in `WEAPON_UPGRADE_SPECS`).

### 3. Measured verification gate (Q3 = B)

- **Record a pre-change baseline** before editing: `npm run evaluate -- --batch
  --games 100` (full campaign, the batch default) with its `balance-report.json`
  / `.txt` retained as the comparison artefact.
- **Run the same batch after the change** and compare (`--tune`-style or a
  documented side-by-side of the aggregate metrics); record the before/after
  numbers in the work item and in the balancing documentation.
- **Expected direction**: the run's build power falls, so the campaign metrics
  move down — `waveReached`, `levelReached` and/or `survivalSeconds` decrease
  (or the run reaches no further) within the documented tolerance. If the game
  becomes unwinnable or the metrics do not move, retune **inside** the stated
  bounds and re-measure (the tune loop is the intended tool).
- **Re-baseline the intended experience** if a band moves materially:
  regenerate `src/data/experience-targets.json` (bumping `targetsVersion`) and
  update GDD §2.7 in the **same** change, so the narrative and the artefact
  never disagree.
- The batch is deterministic for a fixed seed, so the comparison is
  reproducible; the tune loop's same-sweep guard must be respected (no
  campaign-vs-skirmish diffing).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — Strength budget documented.** The pre-change level-0 output table
  (above) and the post-change table, the per-family "output" definition, and the
  level-0 / level-1 / level-cap ceilings are recorded beside the data
  (`WEAPON_CATALOGUE` / `WEAPON_UPGRADE_SPECS` comments) and in GDD §4.4 / §4.4.2,
  so a future weapon can be checked against the same budget.
- [ ] **AC2 — Level-0 trim (40 %).** For **every** non-cannon weapon the
  resolved level-0 output is **≤ 60 % of its AC1 baseline**, and no non-cannon
  weapon's level-0 single-target output exceeds **1.5× the cannon's**; the
  cannon's level-0 values (`offsets`, `fireRateMs`, `bulletLifetime`, any
  `aoe`/`bounce`/`splits`/`maxHitPoints` budget) are byte-identical to today.
  Asserted by a table-driven catalogue test that computes each weapon's output
  from the catalogue and compares against literal baseline values.
- [ ] **AC3 — Curve flattened (all weapons, cannon levels included).**
  `WEAPON_UPGRADE_SPECS` is retuned so that: `resolveWeaponAtLevel(id, 1).projectileCount === 1`
  for every non-orbit projectile weapon (orbit weapons grow pods by exactly +1
  instead); the resolved **level-1 output ≤ 2.5× level-0** and the **saturated
  level-cap output ≤ 50 % of the pre-change level-cap output** for every weapon
  including the cannon pattern; every spec keeps a finite cap, monotonic
  non-decreasing levels, and fire rates stay exact beat subdivisions
  (`isOnBeatGrid`). Asserted in `src/utils/weaponLevels.test.ts`.
- [ ] **AC4 — Acquisition cadence explicitly unchanged.** The producer chose the
  curve lever, not the frequency lever, so `DEFAULT_MINERAL_HOLD_CAPACITY`
  (5), `DEFAULT_MINERAL_HOLD_GROWTH_MULTIPLIER` (2),
  `OWNED_UPGRADE_BONUS_WEIGHT` (1.35) and the unbounded temporary field-pickup
  stacking are **unchanged**, asserted by their existing suites (this AC exists
  to prevent scope creep into pacing).
- [ ] **AC5 — Parity preserved.** The game and every gym consume the same
  catalogue and resolver with no divergent copies; the duplicate-body guard
  (`src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts`), the gym-parity docs
  assertion and the leveling gyms still pass, and `docs/GYM_PARITY.md` still
  describes the shipped behaviour.
- [ ] **AC6 — Measured before/after evidence recorded.** A pre-change
  `npm run evaluate -- --batch --games 100` baseline and a post-change batch of
  the same shape are compared; the before/after aggregate metrics (at least
  `survivalSeconds`, `waveReached`, `levelReached`, `upgradesSelected`) are
  recorded in a work-item comment and in `docs/BALANCING.md`; the campaign
  metrics move in the intended (downward) direction; if a target band moves
  materially, `src/data/experience-targets.json` is re-baselined (`targetsVersion`
  bumped) and GDD §2.7 updated in the same change.
- [ ] **AC7 — Documentation updated.** GDD §2.3 / §4.4 weapon tables, §4.4.2
  level table, per-variable rationale and worked example, plus `README.md`
  weapon/gym notes and any docs that quote a fire rate, pattern count or AOE
  radius, reflect the new values; code comments carry the rationale beside each
  new number.
- [ ] **AC8 — Full project test suite passes** with the new changes (the dev-push
  gate is the enforcement point; no CI/CD pipeline tests are added).

## Constraints

- **Cannon level 0 frozen**; the flatter curve applies to its levels (Q2 answer).
- **Beat-grid invariant is untouchable**: every fire rate remains an exact
  subdivision/multiple of the 80 BPM beat; a "40 % slower cadence" is expressed
  as the nearest on-grid subdivision **at or below** the target.
- **Single source of truth**: changes belong in `WEAPON_CATALOGUE`,
  `DEFAULT_WEAPON_SUBDIVISIONS`, `WEAPON_BULLET_LIFETIME`, `AOE_RADII`,
  `CLUSTER_BASE_WARHEADS` / hit budgets and `WEAPON_UPGRADE_SPECS`; no
  scene-local constants.
- **No acquisition-pacing change** (hold capacity, growth multiplier,
  owned-upgrade weight, temporary stacking all stay) — AC4.
- **No enemy/health compensation** in this work item (Q1 answer is a weapon-side
  trim; if the batch gate shows the game is too hard, re-tune weapons inside the
  bounds rather than buffing enemies here).
- **Gym↔game parity** (AH-0MUGZDTFX004RBD1): gyms inherit the change without
  edits; an intentional divergence needs a recorded reason.
- **Determinism**: the eval batch stays byte-identical for the same seed.
- **Baseline ordering**: the pre-change batch must be captured **before** the
  data edits, otherwise the comparison is meaningless.

## Existing state

- Weapon data: `src/utils/weapons.ts` — 16-weapon catalogue, subdivisions,
  bullet lifetimes, AOE radii, hit budgets, bounce/split/orbit descriptors.
- Level maths: `src/utils/weaponLevels.ts` — `WEAPON_UPGRADE_SPECS` (16
  variables, four shipped: fire rate, projectiles, bullet size, area), the
  exponential-saturation curve, beat quantisation, `resolveWeaponDefinition`.
- Acquisition: `src/core/rules.ts` (`mineralHoldCapacity` 5,
  `mineralHoldGrowthMultiplier` 2, `beatBpm`, `weaponSubdivisions`),
  `src/powerups/choice.ts` (`OWNED_UPGRADE_BONUS_WEIGHT` 1.35),
  `src/entities/Player.ts` (permanent/temporary stack split).
- Measurement: `scripts/evaluate.mjs` batch mode, `src/ai/eval/*`,
  `src/data/experience-targets.json`, `docs/BALANCING.md`,
  `docs/EXPERIENCE_VALIDATION.md`.
- Observation surfaces: `GymWeapons`, `GymWeaponLeveling`, `GymPowerUps*`.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/utils/weapons.ts` — base per-weapon subdivisions, pattern counts,
  lifetimes, hit budgets and AOE radii: the 40 % level-0 trim plus the strength
  budget comment.
- `src/utils/weaponLevels.ts` — `WEAPON_UPGRADE_SPECS` bases, caps and `k` for
  `fireRate`, `projectileCount`, `bulletSize`, `aoeRadius`, plus their
  `rationale` text.
- `src/utils/weaponLevels.test.ts` — level-1 step (+1 projectile), level-1
  output ceiling, level-cap ceiling, monotonicity, beat-grid quantisation.
- `src/utils/weapons.test.ts` — catalogue table test for the trimmed level-0
  values and the 1.5× cannon ceiling.
- `src/scenes/core/optionsEscort.ts` — pod-count growth follows the lowered
  `projectileCount` cap (assert `resolveOptionsPodCount` stays consistent).
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — §2.3, §4.4 weapon tables, §4.4.2 level table
  + rationale + worked example, §2.7 targets narrative if re-baselined.
- `docs/BALANCING.md` — the recorded before/after batch comparison.
- `src/data/experience-targets.json` — **only if** the batch gate shows a band
  moving materially (then `targetsVersion` bump + GDD §2.7 in the same change).
- `README.md` — weapon/gym text quoting fire rates, pattern counts or radii.

## Related work

- **Reduce the starting range of all weapons by 50%** (AH-0MUU131PU006O7ZD) —
  the closest precedent: a blanket catalogue-wide weapon nerf expressed as
  halved base constants, with unit-test ACs and a "levels unchanged" clause.
- **Smart Bomb is too powerful** (AH-0MV8GPGBL009M0D8) — precedent for a
  too-strong-item nerf with explicit before/after numbers and doc updates.
- **Swarm are too powerful when shooting** (AH-0MU0F1T2H003B4K0) — precedent
  for tuning a power source down rather than buffing the opposition.
- **Weapon leveling** (AH-0MUPMPCB2009J54J) — the epic that introduced the
  upgrade curve; **Permanent mineral-choice weapon leveling**
  (AH-0MUQOVYZU0073OUV), **F3: Weapon temporary/permanent split**
  (AH-0MUX9T7C7003CBQP) and **Refactor weapon fire rates as beat subdivisions
  and add catalogue-wide invariant** (AH-0MUGQBN5T009U4YG) define the seams this
  change edits.
- **5 net-new weapon types** (AH-0MVCRC52P001YIPW) and **Area of effect
  weapons** (AH-0MUOOB3OR001V8CD) — the newest catalogue entries whose level-0
  numbers this change touches (shard_swarm 2.5× cannon).
- **Automated balancing** (AH-0MV81Z2EJ006HD5T), **Extend balance harness for
  per-level campaign runs** (AH-0MVLJFB1I0099X4Z) and **Periodically validate
  the human experience against the intended experience** (AH-0MV7WVHU0000U775) —
  the measurement machinery the Q3 = B gate uses.
- **Limit the number of powerup slots** (AH-0MVLIJT3M005HPHF) and **Not all
  power-ups are appearing in the hull-full screen** (AH-0MVI4KTD8000FBJ7) — the
  choice/acquisition path that is deliberately **out of scope** here (AC4).
- **Related docs**: `docs/Game Design Document.md` §2.3, §2.7, §4.4, §4.4.2;
  `docs/BALANCING.md`; `docs/EXPERIENCE_VALIDATION.md`; `docs/GYM_PARITY.md`;
  `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` §5.1.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk — over-nerf at 40 %.** A 40 % output cut is a large move; levels 1–2
  may become tight before the enemy curves catch up. Mitigations: every value
  stays data-driven and trivially retunable, the batch gate (AC6) catches an
  unwinnable campaign, and the tune loop can iterate inside the stated bounds.
- **Risk — quantisation undermines the target.** The beat grid and integer
  pattern counts cannot express an exact 60 %, so some weapons land at 50 %.
  Mitigation: the AC bound is "≤ 60 %" and the realised percentage is recorded
  per weapon; do not loosen the bound to make the arithmetic neat.
- **Risk — pierce/budget identity loss.** Cutting a hit-point budget or a
  bounce turns a signature weapon into a plain shot; mitigated by preferring
  the cadence lever and by the railgun exception (budget is its only lever at a
  3 s cadence).
- **Risk — the bot baseline does not represent human play.** The headless batch
  records ~2 upgrades and `waveReached` 6.46 per run, so the gate is
  **directional** evidence, not proof of feel; a human play-check should follow
  the merge.
- **Risk — experience-targets churn.** Re-baselining is a reviewed artefact
  change (`targetsVersion` bump + GDD §2.7), never a silent edit.
- **Risk — wide but shallow churn.** Catalogue numbers are asserted in several
  suites and quoted across docs; touch only asserted values and their prose.
- **Risk — compounding with power-ups.** Weapon output sits beside already
  re-balanced power-ups (Smart Bomb, Bomb, Shield); if build identity shifts to
  power-ups, record a new work item rather than expanding this one.
- **Assumption A1** — the cannon's level-0 values are frozen; the flatter curve
  still applies to its levels (confirmed by the Q2 answer "applies to both").
- **Assumption A2** — "output" is measured per family as stated in the desired
  change (hits/s, pierce depth × hits/s, coverage area × cadence, pods ×
  cadence).
- **Assumption A3** — a 40 % trim is a single-step change; if the batch gate
  shows under- or over-shoot, retune within the bound rather than introducing a
  second trim pass in this item.
- **Assumption A4** — no enemy or player-health compensation in this item.
- **Assumption A5** — the pre-change batch is captured before any data edit.
- **Assumption A6** — the timed weapon window (`WEAPON_TIMEOUT_MS` 10 s) and
  drop rates are out of scope.

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 — What is the level-0 strength target for non-cannon weapons?**
  Options offered: (A) uniform trim + ~1.5× cannon ceiling, (B) outliers only,
  (C) role caps on multi-target potential.
  **Answer (producer): "A (trim by 40 %)".** A 40 % output cut replaces the
  ~20 % suggested in the draft; the ~1.5× cannon single-target ceiling stands and
  binds for `rapid` (60 % of 3.0× = 1.8×, trimmed further to 1.5×). Source:
  interactive producer reply, 2026-10-30.
- **Q2 — Is "upgrades are too rapid" about step size, frequency, or both?**
  Options offered: (A) step size / flatten the curve, (B) acquisition frequency,
  (C) both.
  **Answer (producer): "A, applies to both"** — the curve lever, and the
  flattened curve applies to the cannon's upgrade levels as well as every other
  weapon (the cannon's level-0 values are explicitly excluded). Source:
  interactive producer reply, 2026-10-30.
  Sub-question "does the flatter curve apply to the cannon's levels?" — answered
  "applies to both"; the level-0 freeze is carried from the seed intent.
- **Q3 — How should "a little" be verified and accepted?**
  Options offered: (A) numeric tests + documented budget, (B) A plus a measured
  batch gate and targets re-baseline, (C) feel-only.
  **Answer (producer): "B".** Acceptance therefore includes the pre/post
  `npm run evaluate -- --batch --games 100` comparison and, where a band moves
  materially, a `targetsVersion` bump in `src/data/experience-targets.json` with
  GDD §2.7 updated in the same change. Source: interactive producer reply,
  2026-10-30.
- **Duplicate-work check** — `wl search` over "weapon upgrade", "too powerful",
  "balance", "upgrade pacing", "weapon level" and "difficulty" returned no
  completed item whose acceptance criteria cover this change. The two nearest
  items (range halving AH-0MUU131PU006O7ZD, Smart Bomb nerf
  AH-0MV8GPGBL009M0D8) are precedents, not duplicates — neither changes base
  weapon damage output or the upgrade curve. **No overlapping completed item
  found.**

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MUGQBN5T009U4YG** – Refactor weapon fire rates as beat subdivisions and add catalogue-wide invariant (completed)
- **AH-0MTC1TEXR006I5XR** – Weapon power-ups (3 patterns + reset) with auto-fire and weapon gym scene (completed)

# Promo scenario contract tests (test-first)

## Summary

Write the hermetic, browser-free test suite that pins the **enriched promo
scenario contract** — registry ↔ resolver parity, dev-only gating and the new
`kind: 'promo'` resolution — **before** any implementation lands
(privileged TDD requirement of AH-0MVI5XI73000ZVYA). The suite lives first
and is initially RED; the scaffold feature (sibling `Enriched scenario
registry schema and resolver`) turns it green. No gameplay and no browser are
touched; the four existing editorial categories from `EDITORIAL_CONFIG`
(`weapons`, `pickups`, `enemies`, `boss`) are referenced by name only here.

## Requirements & context

- This is the test-first slice of the parent item's AC5 (hermetic tests pin
  registry ↔ resolver parity, each scenario's preset and wave definition, and
  dev-only gating).
- Sea of truth and naming stays `scripts/capture-scenarios.mjs` (plain ESM,
  dependency-free) with types in `scripts/capture-scenarios.d.mts`.
- The existing three scenarios (`boss`, `boss-four-hits`, `defeat`) must keep
  their documented behaviour — the contract tests must not regress them.

**Key Files:**
- `scripts/capture-scenarios.test.ts` — extended parity/contract tests
- `scripts/capture-scenarios.mjs` — registry (read-only in tests here)
- `scripts/capture-scenarios.d.mts` — types (read-only in tests here)

## Deliverables

- Extended hermetic contract tests for the enriched registry shape.
- Parity tests covering a `kind: 'promo'` union member (failing until the
  resolver lands).
- Dev-gating tests proving a promo URL is inert in production builds.

## Dependencies

None (test harness only; may reference the intended contract as specified in
the parent's desired change).

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 (contract):** `scripts/capture-scenarios.test.ts` asserts the enriched
  contract: every registry entry has a non-empty `name` and `effect`, and every
  promo-kind entry carries `preset`, `promoLevel`, optional `seed` and the
  editorial `categories` it evidences — all hermetic, no browser (AC5).
- **AC2 (parity):** Parity tests pin registry ↔ resolver agreement for the new
  union: a resolver value that is no longer registered fails fast at module
  load, and an unregistered `scenario` returns `null` (AC5).
- **AC3 (gating):** A dev-gating test proves a promo-scenario URL resolves
  only when `import.meta.env.DEV` is true and is inert otherwise (AC1/AC5).
- **AC4 (TDD):** The suite is committed while RED and goes fully green only
  after the registry-schema scaffold feature lands (AC5).

## Appendix note

Designed from the parent intake brief (Q1–Q3 answered 2026-10-27); no new
questions required.

## Contract pinned by this item (handoff to AH-0MVM4ED003C8ZC)

The suite in `scripts/capture-scenarios.test.ts` pins the enriched contract
exactly. The scaffold item must match it, then flip each `it.fails` back to
`it` (repo red-before/green-after convention; a leftover `it.fails` fails the
suite as an unexpected pass).

1. **Every registry entry declares `kind`**, one of `boss` | `defeat` | `promo`.
   Existing three keep their names + effects: `boss`, `boss-four-hits` are
   `kind: 'boss'`; `defeat` is `kind: 'defeat'`.
2. **`kind: 'promo'` entries carry** a non-empty `preset` (bot-tuning preset
   name), a non-empty `promoLevel` (level reference resolved by the promo wave
   module), a non-empty `categories` array drawn only from
   `weapons` | `pickups` | `enemies` | `boss`, and an optional integer `seed`
   (uint32, omitted when absent).
3. **`resolveDevScenario` is registry-driven**, not a hardcoded name list: a
   registered promo entry resolves to exactly
   `{ kind: 'promo', preset, promoLevel, categories, seed? }` (no extra fields
   — the test uses `toEqual`); an unregistered/blank name returns `null`.
4. **Module-load fail-fast**: a promo entry violating (2) throws at import of
   `src/core/devScenario`, mirroring the existing registry-drift guard; the
   existing guard (a hardcoded resolver name missing from the registry throws)
   is unchanged and retained by a green test.
5. **`resolveEnabledDevScenario(search)` is the single runtime gate**: it
   returns the resolved scenario only when `import.meta.env.DEV === true` and
   `null` otherwise, so a promo URL is inert in production. This is a small
   additive API (the scaffold adds it; `PlayScene` may adopt it in
   AH-0MVSDM8SE0081WU7) so dev gating is testable hermetically without booting
   Phaser.

Test technique: the promo fixtures are injected with `vi.doMock` +
`vi.resetModules` over `scripts/capture-scenarios.mjs`, so the `kind: 'promo'`
union member is pinned before any real promo entry exists (the catalogue item
authors those later). The green test *fails fast at module load when a resolver
name is no longer registered* also acts as the module-mock sentinel, so a
mock that silently stopped applying cannot make the RED tests vacuous.

RED evidence (this item): with the `it.fails` wrappers temporarily flipped to
`it`, the unit project reported `11 failed | 3716 passed` — exactly the 11
pinned assertions and no unrelated failures. With the wrappers in place the
suite is green: `201 files passed, 3716 passed, 11 expected fail`.

Extend the shared dev-scenario registry and resolver so an entry can carry
**promo metadata** — bot-tuning preset name, promo level reference, optional

- `src/core/devScenario.ts` already derives its supported names from the
  registry and fails fast on drift — extend, don't loosen, that contract.
- Dev-only gating (`import.meta.env.DEV`) is unchanged: production never
  honours the `scenario` parameter (AC1).
- Editorial category vocabulary comes from `EDITORIAL_CONFIG` in

# Promo wave definitions module

## Summary

Add a new **dependency-free promo-scenario data module** holding
hand-authored, `LevelDefinition`-compatible wave definitions for the promo
catalogue (the producer's Q2 answer on AH-0MVI5XI73000ZVYA: hand-author all
new promo-tailored waves). Content is composed **only** from the existing
spawner/movement archetypes (V/diver swarm, centipede, ghost, harvester,
horde, strike, lane traffic, asteroid, mini-boss, boss) — no new gameplay
behaviour, so the gym↔game parity and duplicate-body guards stay quiet.

## Requirements & context

- Plain ESM data (like `scripts/capture-scenarios.mjs`): importable by bare
  Node (capture CLI) and the Vite build with types via a `.d.mts`.
- Each promo level is deterministic for a given seed and maps to ≥1 of the
  four editorial categories (`weapons`, `pickups`, `enemies`, `boss`) via
  per-wave metadata, consumed by the catalogue tests later.
- Waves must be bot-survivable and sustain watchable action; the calibration
  slice (sibling `Calibrate bot survival and 45-second footage`) tunes them
  afterwards — this slice delivers the structure and the validation seam.

**Key Files:**
- `scripts/promo-scenarios.mjs` — hand-authored promo level definitions
- `scripts/promo-scenarios.d.mts` — types for the data
- `scripts/promo-scenarios.test.ts` — hermetic validation tests

## Deliverables

- Promo level data module with exported levels, per-level category metadata
  and seed determinism contract.
- Validation tests: wave-group shape (WaveManager's validator), archetype
  whitelist, determinism per seed, plain-ESM importability.

## Dependencies

- Prereq: `Enriched scenario registry schema and resolver` (data shape + how
  promo level references resolve).

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 (content):** `scripts/promo-scenarios.mjs` exports ≥1
  `LevelDefinition`-compatible promo level per planned catalogue entry, built
  only from existing archetypes/flags — nothing new dynamically spawned
  outside the existing spawner classes (AC2).
- **AC2 (validation):** Hermetic tests run `WaveManager`'s wave-group
  validation over every promo wave, assert the archetype whitelist (no new
  movement class), and prove no duplicate-body guard or gym↔game parity test
  is triggered (AC2/AC5).
- **AC3 (determinism):** Each promo level is a pure function of its seed —

- **AC4 (categories):** Every promo level declares ≥1 editorial category key
  from `EDITORIAL_CONFIG`, and the module is readable by the compile-promo
  category vocabulary (AC3).
- **AC5 (portability):** The module imports cleanly in bare Node and in the
  Vite build (mirroring the registry parity pattern) (AC2).

## Appendix note

Designed from the parent intake brief (Q1–Q3 answered 2026-10-27); no new
questions required.
