## Summary

Wire the promo scenario through the game at run start: a `kind: 'promo'`
dev scenario forces **demo/bot mode** (the Watch Demo bot pilots), injects
the scenario's hand-authored promo level as the run campaign, applies the
scenario's bot-tuning **preset by name**, and seeds the run from the
scenario's seed — all through existing seams only, dev-gated exactly like
today's scenarios (AC1/AC2/AC5).

## Requirements & context

- `PlayScene.create()` already resolves and applies dev scenarios via
  `_applyDevScenarioFromUrl()` (line ~1100); the promo path must be applied
  **before** `_applyBotTuning()` (line ~955) and `waveManager.beginGame()`
  (line ~1077) so the preset and campaign are live from frame one — resolve
  the URL early in `create()`/`init` and let the normal campaign block prefer
  the scenario's promo level.
- Promo runs are **bot-flown** (parent AC2): the scene must set
  `demoMode`-equivalent flight when a promo scenario is active so
  `getBotInput()` supplies bot input — without requiring a human pilot.
- The existing `boss` / `defeat` scenarios keep their freeze/release behaviour
  unchanged (backward compatibility).
- Campaign injection reuses `waveManager.setLevels(...)`; preset application
  reuses `getBotTuningConfig(name)` + the `toCompetentOverrides` /
  `toHumanOverrides` mapping already used by `_applyBotTuning`.

**Key Files:**
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — promo application seam at run start
- `src/core/devScenario.ts` — `kind: 'promo'` union member + URL resolution
- `src/scenes/PromoScenario.integration.test.ts` — new bot-flight integration
  test (mirrors `demoMode.integration.test.ts`)
- `src/waves/WaveManager.ts` — read-only reference (injected campaign)

## Deliverables

- Early URL resolution + promo application in `PlayScene` (campaign, preset,
  seed, bot flight).
- Integration/demo check proving a promo scenario is bot-flown with the
  injected campaign and preset.
- Documentation comments on the new seams.

## Dependencies

- Prereq: `Curated bot-tuning presets for promo scenarios` (preset lookup).
- Prereq: `Promo wave definitions module` (promo level data).

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 (apply):** A `kind: 'promo'` dev scenario starts a run that flies the
  Watch Demo bot, plays the scenario's promo level as the campaign, applies
  the scenario's preset by name, and seeds the RNG from the scenario's seed —
  all present in the first frame (AC2).
- **AC2 (gating):** The promo path is inert in production builds and when no
  promo scenario is requested; normal runs and the existing boss/defeat
  scenarios are byte-for-byte unchanged (AC1).
- **AC3 (integration):** The integration/demo check (new or existing
  demo-mode suite) asserts bot input is honoured, `getBotTuningConfigName()`
  reports the scenario's preset, and the run is seeded deterministically —
  AC5's demo check.
- **AC4 (parity):** Gym↔game parity and duplicate-body guards stay green; no
  new gameplay behaviour is introduced (parity constraint).

## Appendix note

Design decision recorded for the producer: promo scenarios imply bot flight
and therefore force demo-mode flight when active (dev-only). Consistent with
parent AC2 ("bot-pilotable end to end"). No new questions required.

# Capture CLI promo scenario support

## Summary

Teach the capture CLI to drive **bot-flown promo scenarios**: `--scenario
<promo-name>` starts a demo-mode bot run against the scenario's URL and
records until the run-ended signal (bounded by `--max-duration`), with no
freeze/release step; `--list-scenarios` shows each scenario's richer metadata
and `--all-scenarios` still records one clean clip per scenario (AC4).

## Requirements & context

- Existing capture flow distinguishes `demo` (Tab then Enter, waits for
  run-ended) from jump `scenario` kinds (Enter, waits for the page-side
  freeze/release handle). Promo scenarios are continuous bot runs, so their
  lifecycle matches the **demo path**, not the jump path — the launch and
  wait must be selected per scenario kind.
- `--list-scenarios` reads the shared registry (already true); extend the
  formatted effect line with preset/category info without breaking the
  machine-readable JSON list.
- `--all-scenarios` already expands the registry into one clip per scenario
  and must continue to work unchanged for the richer entries.
- Boss/defeat scenario capture must keep its exact behaviour (regression).

**Key Files:**
- `scripts/capture-gameplay.mjs` — launch keys/lifecycle per scenario kind,
  `--help` text
- `scripts/capture-gameplay.test.ts` — unit tests for launch planning,
  listing formatting, batch expansion
- `scripts/capture-scenes.mjs` — read-only reference (scene configs)

## Deliverables

- Scenario-kind-aware capture planning (demo-lifecycle for promo, jump for
  boss/defeat).
- Metadata-rich `--list-scenarios` output and batch run over all scenarios.
- Updated CLI unit tests and `--help`.

## Dependencies

- Prereq: `Apply promo scenarios in PlayScene bot-flight` (scenario runtime
  the CLI drives).

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 (launch):** `--scenario <promo>` starts the demo-mode bot run with the
  scenario URL and records deterministically until run-ended / max-duration —
  no scenario-handle release required (AC4).
- **AC2 (list):** `npm run capture -- --list-scenarios` lists every
  scenario — human and `--json` — with its one-line effect referencing
  category/preset; every registry entry appears (parent AC4).
- **AC3 (batch):** `npm run capture -- --all-scenarios` records one clean
  clip per registered scenario including the promo set, and exits
  non-zero only on genuine failures/caps (parent AC4).
- **AC4 (compat):** `--scenario boss*` / `--scenario defeat` behave exactly as
  before; all CLI unit tests pass (backward compatibility + AC7).

## Appendix note

Design decision: promo scenarios use the demo lifecycle. Consistent with
parent AC4 and the bot-flight decision in sibling `Apply promo scenarios in
PlayScene bot-flight`. No new questions required.

# Calibrate bot survival and 45-second footage

## Summary

Prove — and where needed tune — that the competent bot survives and keeps
producing watchable action for **≥45 s** in every promo scenario before the
demo game-over dwell, using the existing headless AI eval harness rather than
ad-hoc browser captures (AC2's sustained-footage target).

## Requirements & context

- The repo already ships `src/ai/eval/` (`arena.ts`, `engine.ts`) which builds
  the **real campaign** through `buildSequencedLevels` — the same harness can
  fly the competent bot against an injected promo level headlessly.
- A scenario the bot dies in instantly is a wasted clip; a flat set of similar
  archetypes reads as repetitive (parent's recorded risks).
- Calibration knobs are wave composition/count/timing (promo wave data) and
  preset tuning (bot-tuning.json) — **not** new gameplay behaviour.
- Any evidence-gathering long run must follow the shared background-job
  etiquette (launch → prepare → one completion-aware wait).

**Key Files:**
- `src/ai/eval/arena.ts` — read-only harness reference for the check
- `scripts/promo-scenarios.mjs` — wave tuning target
- `src/data/bot-tuning.json` — preset tuning target
- `src/waves/promoScenario.survival.test.ts` — new hermetic survival check

## Deliverables

- A hermetic (no browser) per-scenario survival/duration check with an
  explicit ≥45 s assertion and bounded runtime.
- Tuned wave/preset data so every scenario passes.
- Recorded evidence (measured durations) in the completion comment.

## Dependencies

- Prereq: `Author 10+ promo scenarios by editorial category` (the catalogue
  being measured).

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 (harness):** A hermetic test/script drives the competent bot over each
  promo level via the existing eval harness and reports per-scenario simulated
  action duration before game over (AC2).
- **AC2 (threshold):** Every promo scenario sustains ≥45 s of action before
  the demo game-over dwell; failures name the scenario and measured duration
  (AC2).
- **AC3 (tuning):** Any scenario below threshold is fixed by tuning wave
  composition and/or preset values only — no new spawner behaviour, and the
  gym↔game parity/duplicate-body guards stay green (AC2).
- **AC4 (regression):** The check runs in bounded time as part of the standard
  suite and the full existing suite passes (AC5/AC7).

Designed from the parent intake brief (Q1–Q3 answered 2026-10-27); no new
questions required.

## Problem

Candidate D's *States* section (`docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md` § Candidate D → States) defines a ring win as **all six hexes held and the AI's massed counter-attack on the hangar repelled**, and a campaign loss as **the hangar falls** (the last hex taken and the hangar's own defence failing). The MVP build (AH-0MVU3VNJI00066YE) deliberately ships the narrower rule, decided by the producer on 2026-10-30 (intake question Q2 = a):

- **Ring secured = every hex of the current ring held.** The next ring then opens.
- **No massed hangar assault** is resolved or played.
- **No hangar-falls lose state**: the hangar itself can never be lost in the MVP, so a player cannot lose the campaign.

## Goal (user story)

As a player, I want the ring to end with a real fight for the hangar — a massed AI counter-attack I have to repel, and a defeat condition that means the hangar can actually fall — so that holding the whole ring feels like a victory rather than the start of the next checklist.

## Desired change

- When the last hex of a ring is captured, **resolve an algorithmic hangar assault** from stored numbers (defender ratings of the held ring vs. the AI's massed force scaled by frontier aggression) — no live simulated battle, matching Candidate D's algorithmic-resolution rule.
- A repelled assault = the ring win state (existing) **plus** a legible report of the numbers.
- A failed assault = **the hangar falls**: define the consequence (restart the current ring with the hangar's unlocks kept, or a documented alternative) and make the reset legible in the defence report.
- Record the chosen win/lose semantics in GDD §8 and `docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md`.
- Pure resolver logic, exercised in the existing `GymHexWar` gym; gym↔game parity per AGENTS.md; attract mode must not stall (no live battle).

## Acceptance criteria

1. Capturing the ring's final hex triggers an algorithmic hangar-assault resolution from stored numbers, with a report showing the numbers that produced the result.
2. A repelled assault marks the ring won; a failed assault applies the documented hangar-falls consequence.
3. The resolver is a pure module exercised in the gym, with unit tests for repel, fall and boundary cases, and `docs/GYM_PARITY.md` updated if the gym surface changes.
4. The attract bot traverses or skips the assault report without stalling.
5. GDD §8 and `docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md` record the win/lose semantics; build and full suite green; all related documentation updated.
6. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Context

Deferred by producer decision during intake of AH-0MVU3VNJI00066YE (2026-10-30, question Q2 = a). Design of record: `docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md` Candidate D (States, Minimal first slice) and GDD §8.

# Intake Brief — SFX on mini-boss explosions

**Work item:** AH-0MVVEI7FD004TR2M (feature, medium)
**Headline:** Give the mini-boss defeat explosion sweep its missing audio: the
mini-boss body plays a boss-scale death cue on the defeat frame, every planned
sweep burst fires a cue scheduled to land with its own visual burst (thinned and
voice-limited so ~60 bursts cannot clip the mix), and the 20-burst finale
(2 every 0.25 s) reads as the loudest moment of the sequence.

**Source request (verbatim):** "We have plenty of explosions when the miniboss is
killed, but there are no SFX accompnaying them"

**Producer decisions (settled 2026-10-31, all three answered "A"):**
**Q1 = (a) reuse existing baked cues only** — no new ToneForge recipe or asset;
**Q2 = (a) one cue per burst with per-role thinning** — every escort burst,
every 2nd scatter/anchored burst, both voices of every finale pair;
**Q3 = (a) visual-timed** — each cue scheduled at its burst's own `delayMs`,
never quantised to the 16th-note accent grid.

## Problem statement

Defeating a mini-boss already produces a large visual display — the shared death
sweep (`src/scenes/core/miniBossDeathSweep.ts`) fires one burst per swept escort
plus `max(0, 30 − n)` scattered bursts, 10 anchored bursts around the death point
and a 20-burst finale (two every 250 ms) — but **not one of those bursts makes a
sound**. The mini-boss's own body also dies silently: the mini-boss is not routed
through the shared enemy-kill seam (`finaliseEnemyKill`), so it never reaches
`playDestructionSound()`, and it has no `playDestructionAudio` of its own. The
result is a ~5 s victory moment that plays out in near-silence against a busy
combat mix, so the biggest kill in a level reads as weaker than a routine enemy
kill.

## Users

- **Player** — "As a player, when I finally kill the mini-boss I want the whole
  screen of explosions to *sound* like the biggest thing I have done in the
  level, so the victory lands instead of trickling past."
- **Player (headphones / low volume)** — "As a player, I want the cascade to be
  dense but never a clipped wall of noise, so I can still hear the score, my own
  weapons and the next wave's telegraphs."
- **Developer/tester (gym)** — "As a tester, when I press EXPLODE in the
  mini-boss gym I want to hear exactly the audio that ships in the game, so audio
  parity is verifiable in one click."
- **Producer / audio designer** — "As the producer, I want the cue choices and the
  density policy to be named, tunable constants in one shared place, so I can
  retune the moment without touching gameplay code."

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Every planned burst is voiced, in sync with its visual (Q1=a, Q3=a).**
  The shared sweep is the single audio dispatch point: each planned burst that
  passes the thinning rule dispatches exactly one cue scheduled at that burst's own
  `delayMs` (so audio lands with the burst it belongs to, never on the global
  16th-note grid), and the mini-boss's own body plays `playBossDestructionSound()`
  exactly once on the defeat frame. Neither an unplanned burst nor a burst the
  thinning rule drops ever produces a cue, so the thinning rule is the only reason a
  planned burst is silent.
- **AC2 — Density is bounded and tunable in one place (Q2=a).** The thinning rule
  is per role, exported as `MINI_BOSS_SWEEP_SFX_*` constants with no inline tuning
  literals: **every** `enemy` burst, **every 2nd** `scatter` and `anchored` burst,
  and **both** voices of every `finale` pair (2 per 250 ms). Per-role volume scales
  are exported constants too, with the finale the loudest layer. The existing per-cue
  voice limiter (4 voices / 150 ms) stays the hard backstop; a test asserts the
  dispatch count per 250 ms window stays within the documented bound for the
  maximum 60-burst plan, and that the finale is never thinned.
- **AC3 — Reuse-only, documented cue palette (Q1=a).** No new ToneForge recipe,
  no new baked asset, no manifest change: body → `playBossDestructionSound()`;
  `enemy` / `scatter` / `anchored` bursts → `playDestructionSound()` cue family
  (its 3 baked variants); `finale` bursts → `playVictoryExplosionSound()` (its 4
  baked variants, drawn deterministically from the run seed). The choices are
  recorded in the GDD §7.3 row and are audibly distinct from
  `playPlayerDestructionSound()`; the cue-manifest contract suite still passes
  unchanged.
- **AC4 — Game↔gym parity, no divergent copy.** Both `PlayScene` and `GymMiniBoss`
  get the audio from the one shared executor; neither scene contains its own cue
  logic. The repo duplicate-body guard
  (`src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts`) and the gym-parity docs
  assertion pass.
- **AC5 — Safe no-op and deterministic.** Headless tests, muted SFX, volume 0 and
  autoplay-blocked browsers play nothing and never throw. Cue/seed selection draws
  from the run-seeded RNG carried in the plan (no `Math.random()` in the planner),
  so the same seed replays the same audio; an injectable `playSound` seam lets
  tests record dispatch without audio hardware.
- **AC6 — Validation.** New unit tests cover: one cue per kept burst at the
  burst's delay, the thinning/limit bounds at the 60-burst maximum, the body cue
  firing exactly once, the final-vs-escort volume relation, the no-op/mute paths,
  and seed determinism; the docs tests for the updated GDD §7.3 row pass.
- **AC7 — Documentation.** GDD §7.3 SFX Event Catalog gains a mini-boss-defeat
  row (character, volume, lead time), `docs/AUDIO_TONEFORGE_CUE_MAPPING.md` and
  `docs/GYM_PARITY.md` are updated as applicable, and the module JSDoc records the
  density policy and the reason for any divergence from the 16th-note accent grid.
- **AC8 — Full project test suite must pass with the new changes**, via the
  dev-push gate (never an ad-hoc full run).
- **AC9 — The victory hold is not delayed (constraint).** Audio never gates the
  sweep's completion: `onComplete` still fires from the last burst's own tween as
  today, with SFX enabled, with SFX muted/blocked by autoplay policy and when the
  injected `playSound` seam throws, so the reward-overlay hold of
  AH-0MVOFGB6K003YD0Z (AC3/AC6) is unchanged. A test asserts `onComplete` fires
  exactly once in each of those cases and that no cue is dispatched after the
  sweep handle is `stop()`ped.

## Constraints

- Audio is build-time baked ToneForge WAVs played through the single shared
  `AudioContext`; no procedural synthesis (the thruster hum is the only
  exception). **Reuse-only (Q1=a): no new recipe, no new bake, no manifest change.**
- The planner must stay Phaser-free, pure, total and deterministic — the cue
  choice belongs in the plan; only the executor talks to the scene.
- The sweep is cosmetic: no gameplay, score, drop, telemetry or wave-accounting
  change, and the reward overlay hold (parent AC3/AC6 of AH-0MVOFGB6K003YD0Z)
  must be unaffected — audio must not delay `onComplete`.
- The mini-boss must never acquire audio by being routed through the
  reward-bearing enemy-kill seam (that would resurrect score/drop/telemetry for
  swept entities, forbidden by AH-0MVOFGB6K003YD0Z AC4).
- Gym↔game parity is mandatory (AGENTS.md); any intentional divergence must be
  recorded on this item and in a code comment.

## Existing state

- `src/scenes/core/miniBossDeathSweep.ts` — shared planner + executor, consumed by
  `PlayScene._damageMiniBoss` (`src/scenes/PlayScene.ts:3272`) and
  `GymMiniBoss.explodeRandom` (`src/scenes/gym/GymMiniBoss.ts:315`). Bursts carry
  `role: 'enemy' | 'scatter' | 'anchored' | 'finale'`, `delayMs`, position,
  colour, `particleCount`, `scale`, `lifespanMs`. **No audio anywhere**; the only
  injectable seam is `options.onComplete`.
- `src/entities/MiniBoss.ts` — no audio of any kind; `takeDamage()`/`destroySelf()`
  are silent, and swept escorts are removed via `destroySilently()` (no cue).
- `src/audio/effects.ts` — the cue layer. Relevant existing cues:
  `playDestructionSound()` (enemy fall, beat-quantised via `playExplosionCue`),
  `playBossDestructionSound()` (0.6 s saw 180→20 Hz, the full boss death),
  `playVictoryExplosionSound()` / `playVictoryCrackSound()` /
  `playVictoryPopSound()` (multi-seed, `options.delay` + `options.volume`),
  `playPlayerDestructionSound()`. Volume-scale constant precedent:
  `TANK_SCOUT_FIRE_VOLUME_SCALE`, `PHASER_FIRE_VOLUME_SCALE`,
  `HOLD_FULL_FIRE_VOLUME_SCALE`.
- `src/audio/cueVoiceLimiter.ts` — per-cue cap of 4 voices per 150 ms applied once
  at the `playCue` funnel.
- `src/vfx/endOfRunJuice.ts` — precedent for sounding a multi-burst display:
  a per-burst sound player seam (`playVictoryFireworkCue`), a per-play volume and
  an `ENDOFRUN_VICTORY_FIREWORKS_SOUND_EVERY_N` thinning knob (currently `1`).
- Docs: GDD §7.3 (SFX Event Catalog + beat-synced accents),
  `docs/AUDIO_TONEFORGE_CUE_MAPPING.md`, `docs/AUDIO_ENEMY_BALANCE.md`
  (heavy-one-shot RMS tier 0.090, peaks ≤ 0.50), `docs/GYM_PARITY.md`.

## Desired change

1. Extend the pure planner so each planned burst carries its audio decision
   (cue + baked-variant seed + volume scale + whether the thinning rule keeps it),
   derived from its `role`, the run seed and the thinning rule — so the plan stays
   deterministic and fully testable without Phaser. Settled palette (Q1=a):
   `enemy`/`scatter`/`anchored` → `playDestructionSound` family;
   `finale` → `playVictoryExplosionSound` family.
2. Extend the executor with an injectable sound seam
   (`options.playSound?: (burst, cue) => void`) defaulting to a real dispatcher in
   `src/audio/effects.ts` (e.g. `playMiniBossSweepSound(role, options)`), scheduling
   each kept cue at the burst's own `delayMs` (Q3=a, visual-timed) — the same way
   `spawnVictoryFireworks` schedules its cues.
3. Play `playBossDestructionSound()` for the mini-boss body on the defeat frame,
   from the same shared seam, exactly once.
4. Export the tunables (`MINI_BOSS_SWEEP_SFX_ENABLED`, per-role volume scales,
   per-role thinning (
   `enemy` 1, `scatter` 2, `anchored` 2, `finale` 1), voice budget) as constants in
   the sweep module and document them in the module JSDoc.
5. Tests + docs as listed in the ACs.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/scenes/core/miniBossDeathSweep.ts` — plan gains a per-burst audio descriptor (`cue`, variant seed, volume, kept-by-thinning); executor gains the `playSound` seam and schedules each kept cue at the burst `delayMs`; new exported SFX tunables.
- `src/scenes/core/miniBossDeathSweep.test.ts` — one cue per kept burst at the right delay, thinning/limit bounds at 60 bursts, finale never thinned, body cue once, determinism, no-op seam.
- `src/audio/effects.ts` — role→cue dispatcher (`playMiniBossSweepSound`) + volume constants, built on the existing `playCue` options; no new synthesis, no manifest change.
- `src/audio/effects.test.ts` / `src/audio/effects.contract.test.ts` — dispatcher coverage: cue mapping, volume scaling, mute/volume-0 no-op, never throws.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` §7.3 — new mini-boss-defeat SFX row (character, volume, lead time) and a note on why the cascade is visual-timed rather than 16th-note-quantised.
- `docs/AUDIO_TONEFORGE_CUE_MAPPING.md` — record that the sweep reuses existing cues (no new recipe/asset).
- `docs/GYM_PARITY.md` — `GymMiniBoss` row note that the sweep's audio is shared (only if the row's wording needs it).

> `src/audio/cueManifest.ts` / `src/audio/cueManifest.test.ts` are **not**
> modified either: the cue-manifest contract suite is the guard that proves the
> palette is reuse-only (Q1=a) — it must keep passing unchanged.
>
> `src/entities/MiniBoss.ts` and `docs/AUDIO_ENEMY_BALANCE.md` are **not** touched:
> the body cue is dispatched from the shared defeat seam and no asset is baked
> (Q1=a).

## Related work

- **AH-0MVOFGB6K003YD0Z — Mini Boss explosions** (completed, high): the parent
  request that created the visual sweep (scope split, 30 extras, 10 anchored,
  20-burst finale, reward held until completion). This item adds the audio layer to
  exactly that display and must not change its timings or the reward hold.
- **AH-0MVROEKMT005RVML — PlayScene mini-boss defeat sweep wiring**,
  **AH-0MVROEJJR002HDLS — Verification tests for mini-boss death sweep**,
  **AH-0MVROELN600410GP — PlayScene mini-boss defeat sweep wiring**,
  **AH-0MVROEMUO007Z3RY (GymMiniBoss sweep)**,
  **AH-0MVROEO2I0014ILM — Mini-boss defeat sweep documentation** (all completed):
  the module, its tests, its scene wiring and its docs that this change extends.
- **AH-0MV01HNLU008S5E3 — Explosions timed with the beat** (completed): the
  16th-note accent quantisation + per-tick cap used by enemy destruction cues; this
  item departs from it for the sweep (display-timed) and must say so.
- **AH-0MVH8RQR7007QG8E — Limit the number of each explosion and weapon sound that
  can fire** (completed): the per-cue voice limiter that is the cascade's hard
  backstop.
- **AH-0MUWZ5HCV0034H44 — Massive Explosions and Fireworks on Victory** (completed):
  the precedent for per-burst SFX on a planned multi-burst display
  (`playVictoryFireworkCue`, per-play volume, `..._SOUND_EVERY_N` thinning).
- **AH-0MVAUU594007S92Q — Balance the levels of all enemy sounds** /
  **AH-0MVCRR10A001OM2K** (completed): the heavy-one-shot RMS tier (0.090) and peak
  ceilings a new cue must respect.
- **AH-0MUTUOB7X007PR9J — Switch game audio from procedural Web Audio to
  ToneForge** (completed): the baked-asset-only constraint.
- **AH-0MVJ8TB610098DSY — Explosions should be explosions** (open, medium): the
  visual counterpart; if it changes burst visuals, the audio timing here is
  unaffected (audio is driven by `delayMs`, not by burst shape).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk — cacophony.** 60 bursts over ~5 s voiced naively is a clipped wall;
  mitigated by per-role thinning, per-role volume scales and the existing 4-voice /
  150 ms per-cue limiter, all pinned by a test at the 60-burst maximum.
- **Risk — audio/visual desync.** Using the beat-quantised
  `playExplosionCue` seam would shift cues up to 187.5 ms off their bursts and drop
  most of them at the 4-per-tick cap; the settled decision (Q3=a) is to schedule by
  `delayMs` (visual-timed), recorded as a deliberate departure in the GDD row.
- **Risk — the mini-boss body cue steals the finale's impact.** If the body cue is
  the loudest element on frame 0, the 20-burst finale stops reading as a climax;
  mitigated by the settled per-role volume scales making the finale the loudest
  per-burst layer (Q2/Q3 = a).
- **Risk — the sweeps regain reward semantics.** Voicing the mini-boss through
  `finaliseEnemyKill` would award score/drops/telemetry; the shared defeat seam is
  used instead (AH-0MVOFGB6K003YD0Z AC4).
- **Risk — pausing.** Cues scheduled with `delay` must not outlive a scene
  shutdown mid-sweep; dispatch at spawn time (Phaser handles the schedule) and rely
  on the existing scene-teardown mute path, asserted by a test.
- **Assumption —** no new asset is needed (Q1 = a, settled): the existing cue
  families already cover the moment.
- **Assumption —** the audio is dispatched from the shared sweep seam, not from
  `PlayScene`/`GymMiniBoss`, because parity is mandatory.
- **Scope-creep guard.** A per-burst voice-limiter retune, any new recipe
  (explicitly declined in Q1), background music for the mini-boss
  (AH-0MVKXT7O70061FXU) and any visual change to the sweep are **out of scope**;
  they are recorded as linked work items rather than absorbed here.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1 (ANSWERED): Which cue palette? — Answer (producer, interactive reply
  2026-10-31): **(a) reuse existing baked cues only** — body
  `playBossDestructionSound`, sweep bursts `playDestructionSound`, finale
  `playVictoryExplosionSound`; no new ToneForge recipe or asset. Options offered:
  (a) reuse only; (b) reuse + a new dedicated `playMiniBossDestructionSound`
  recipe; (c) reuse but one heavy `playBossDestructionSound()` climax. Agent's
  advisory recommendation was (a). Source: producer reply on this item.
- Q2 (ANSWERED): How dense should the cascade be? — Answer (producer, interactive
  reply 2026-10-31): **(a) one cue per burst with per-role thinning** — every
  escort burst, every 2nd scatter/anchored burst, both voices of every finale pair.
  Options offered: (a) per-burst with thinning; (b) per-burst with no thinning;
  (c) body + finale pairs only. Agent's advisory recommendation was (a). Source:
  producer reply on this item.
- Q3 (ANSWERED): Visual-timed or beat-quantised? — Answer (producer, interactive
  reply 2026-10-31): **(a) visual-timed** — each cue scheduled at its burst's own
  `delayMs`; the sweep does not route through the 16th-note accent grid. Options
  offered: (a) visual-timed; (b) beat-quantised. Agent's advisory recommendation
  was (a). Source: producer reply on this item.
- Q4 (answered from repo context, no producer input needed): Should the gym get the
  audio too? — **Yes**; AGENTS.md gym↔game parity is mandatory and
  `GymMiniBoss.explodeRandom` already runs the shared executor, so the audio comes
  from the shared module. Source: `docs/GYM_PARITY.md` (GymMiniBoss row),
  `src/scenes/gym/GymMiniBoss.ts:315`.
- Q5 (answered from repo context): Is there already a mini-boss death cue to reuse?
  — **No**: `src/entities/MiniBoss.ts` has no audio and the GDD §7.3 catalog has no
  mini-boss-defeat row. Source: repo search for `sound|audio|cue` in
  `src/entities/MiniBoss.ts` and `docs/Game Design Document.md` §7.3.
- Q6 (answered from repo context): Must the audio be baked assets rather than
  procedural? — **Yes**; procedural Web Audio was removed
  (AH-0MUTUOB7X007PR9J), the thruster hum is the only runtime-synthesised
  exception. Source: GDD §7.3.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MVOFGB6K003YD0Z** – Mini Boss explosions (completed)
- **AH-0MVCRBISU006NUN5** – PlayScene mini-boss integration (completed)

# Loadout can exceed the six-slot cap (HUD shows more than six equipped upgrades/weapons)

**Issue type:** bug · **Priority:** high · **Reported:** 2026-10-30 (operator, normal play)

**Headline:** A fresh run's HUD upgrade list shows more than six equipped kinds (a mix of permanent `∞` rows and timed countdown rows) even though the shared six-slot cap says a run can never hold more than six distinct kinds. The shared gate looks complete on inspection, so either an acquisition surface bypasses it or the HUD presents non-slot state as equipped (exempt Mystery UFO, residual Phase Shift/Teleport charges, a Teleport-arrival Phase row). Establish which from a recording, close any real bypass, and make the displayed loadout agree with the six-slot model.

## Problem statement

The six-slot cap (parent AH-0MVLIJT3M005HPHF) promises that "a run can never hold more than six distinct kinds at once, however they were acquired" (GDD §4.4 "Loadout slots"). In a fresh run the operator nevertheless sees more than six upgrade entries in the in-game HUD list, with a **mix of permanent (`∞`) and timed (countdown) rows**, and believes the extra entries also **function** in play — so the loadout reads as genuinely over the cap.

## Users

- **Player** — "As a player, I want the upgrade list to show exactly what my ship is carrying and to make the six-slot limit legible, so I can trust that the cap is real and plan what to collect."
- **Developer/maintainer** — "As a developer, I want one seam that decides slot occupancy and one display that cannot claim more slots than the model allows, so a seventh kind can never be acquired or shown as equipped."

## Existing state (verified in code, `dev` @ 40314aeb)

Cap model (`src/powerups/slots.ts`, `POWER_UP_SLOT_CAP = 6` in `src/core/constants.ts`):

- `resolveSlotState()` derives occupancy from four snapshots — `PowerUpLevelStore.getLevels()` / `getTempPowerUpIds()` and `Player.getWeaponLevels()` / `getTempWeaponIds()`. A kind is held while permanent **or** while a field-pickup window is open (producer Q4a), so temporary stacks count.
- `availableWhenSlotsFull` entries (**Extra Life**, **Mystery UFO**) and the slot-exempt `reset` utility never count (producer Q7a); the permanent `cannon` is excluded.
- `used` is a count of distinct counted kinds, and `isFull` is `used >= 6`.

Gate surfaces (all consume the shared helper):

- drop draw — `drawNextDrop` in `src/scenes/core/dropLayer.ts`,
- field collection — `CombatCoreScene._canCollectDrop` → `isWithinSlotPool` (`_collectOverlappingDrops` / `_updateDropLayer`),
- hold-full choice — `buildChoiceCandidates` in `src/powerups/choice.ts`,
- mini-boss reward unlock half — filtered in `PlayScene.openMiniBossReward` via `filterOptionsWithinSlotPool`.

Surfaces with **no** slot gate (by design or otherwise — audit target):

- checkpoint resume — `PlayScene._restoreCheckpoint()` replays stored **permanent** grants; today it cannot add a new kind beyond the saved six, but it is not gated and relies on the saved state being valid,
- capture/scripted setups — `src/scenes/core/sceneSetup.ts` applies arbitrary `weapons` / `weaponLevels` / `powerUps` straight through `Player.equipWeapon` / `Player.collectPowerUp` (gym and video-capture surface, AH-0MVRMHYJR000Y9H8).

HUD presentation (`src/ui/HUD.ts` — **not** the slot model):

- `refresh()` rebuilds rows every frame: one row per visible power-up (`_buildPowerUpRows()` + `_isPowerUpRowVisible()`) then one row per `registry.activeWeapons()`.
- There is no row ceiling, no slot indicator and no distinction between rows that consume a slot and rows that do not. Rows that can appear while holding **no** slot:
  - **Mystery UFO** — exempt (`availableWhenSlotsFull`), row shown while `powerUpLevel > 0`;
  - **Phase Shift** — row shown while `isActive('phase_shift')`, which a **Teleport arrival** opens without owning Phase Shift, and while `phaseCharges() > 0`, which persists after the field-pickup level window expires (Resolved decision 1b: granted charges are never clawed back);
  - **Teleport** — same residual-stack rule via `teleportStacks() > 0`;
  - Extra Life has no row (dedicated lives counter).
- A six-kind loadout plus any one of those reads as seven or more "equipped" upgrades.

Observability:

- `npm run record` (`scripts/record-session.mjs`) records a real (or bot) session to JSONL through `src/telemetry`: a `run_header`, per-tick state (including permanent `weaponLevels` / `powerUpLevels` via `PlayScene._telemetryExtras()`) and discrete events — `pickup { kind, id }`, `hold_full { options }`, `choice_selected { index, id }`. A recording therefore pins down exactly which kinds were collected and when; `scripts/analyse-recording.mjs` and `scripts/inspect-telemetry.mjs` read them. See `docs/TELEMETRY.md`.

Test coverage today: `src/powerups/slots.test.ts`, `src/powerups/slots.parity.test.ts` and `src/ui/HUD.test.ts` cover the model and row building separately — **nothing** asserts a HUD row ceiling or cross-checks the rendered rows against `resolveSlotState()`.

## Desired change

1. Establish the true cause from a recorded fresh-run session: which of the > 6 rows were **slot-counted** and which were display-only (exempt entry / residual charge pool / Teleport-arrival phase).
2. If any acquisition surface can add a seventh slot-counted kind, gate it through the shared helper (one implementation, no scene-local copies) and cover it with a regression test.
3. Make the player-visible loadout agree with the six-slot model: the HUD must never present more than six slot-counted rows as equipped, and must make non-slot rows legible as such (an exempt marker, a separate "always available" grouping, or an explicit `n/6` slot budget — the exact presentation is settled at review and recorded on the item).
4. Keep the cap's chosen semantics intact — temporary pickups still occupy a slot while their window is open (Q4a), exempt entries still never count (Q7a), the hold-full choice still offers only what is in the slots (Q6a), and no field pickup outlives its per-upgrade TTL (AH-0MVUGI5P2001C1IL).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Reproduction and characterisation.** A recorded fresh-run session (`npm run record`, operator-supplied path) or an equivalent scene test captures the state where the HUD shows more than six upgrade rows; each row is classified as slot-counted or non-slot (exempt entry / residual charge pool / Teleport-arrival phase) and the classification is recorded as a comment on this item with the evidence path (recording file or test name).
2. **No acquisition surface can exceed six counted kinds.** Field collection, the shared drop draw, the hold-full choice, the mini-boss unlock half, checkpoint resume and capture/scene setups are each checked against the shared helper; a test per surface proves a seventh distinct **counted** kind cannot be acquired (or, for a surface that must intentionally diverge, the divergence is documented with its reason). `resolveSlotState(...).used <= POWER_UP_SLOT_CAP` is asserted as an invariant for a mixed permanent + temporary loadout.
3. **The displayed loadout agrees with the model.** For a mixed permanent + countdown loadout the HUD's slot-counted rows equal `resolveSlotState().used` and never exceed `POWER_UP_SLOT_CAP`; non-slot rows are visibly distinguished from equipped kinds (or replaced by an explicit slot budget). Asserted by a HUD/scene test over a loadout that includes an exempt entry and a residual charge pool.
4. **Regression guard on the reported scenario.** The scenario from AC1 (replayed recording or fixture) no longer shows more than six slot-counted rows; if a genuine bypass was found, the failing surface is covered by a test that fails on the pre-fix code.
5. **Documentation and suite.** GDD §4.4 "Loadout slots" and `docs/BALANCING.md` "The six loadout slots" are updated to state how the HUD presents occupancy and non-slot rows; all related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **One rule, one implementation.** The fix belongs in `src/powerups/slots.ts` or its shared consumers (`dropLayer`, `CombatCoreScene`, `choice`, `HUD`) — no per-scene or per-gym copy (gym↔game parity, AH-0MUGZDTFX004RBD1).
- **Keep the producer decisions.** Do not weaken Q4a (temporary pickups hold a slot), Q5b (blocked pickups stay on the field with the blocked cue), Q6a (the choice offers only what is in the slots) or Q7a (exempt entries never count).
- **No second HUD data path.** Rows keep coming from `EffectsRegistry` through the existing `HUD.refresh()`; a slot indicator must be derived from the same shared helper.
- **No behaviour change below the cap** — spawning, collection and choice behaviour with fewer than six held kinds must be identical.
- **No TTL regressions** — a field pickup still expires on its per-upgrade window (AH-0MVUGI5P2001C1IL) and a permanent grant still never strands a temporary stack (AH-0MVUGI4IC006PUS5).
- **Capture setups are not normal play** — if gating `sceneSetup.ts` would break the scripted video scenes (AH-0MVPJ3NSK008V5VB), document the divergence and its reason instead of leaving it silent.
- **Repository boundaries** — only `src/` and `docs/` change; do not edit `.pi/`, `skill/`, `command/` or other agent infrastructure.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/powerups/slots.ts` — the occupancy rule and gates; add any missing predicate or invariant helper here.
- `src/ui/HUD.ts` — `refresh()`, `_buildPowerUpRows()`, `_isPowerUpRowVisible()`, `_powerUpStacks()`, `_ownsChargePool()`; where slot-counted vs non-slot presentation must be decided.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts` — `_canCollectDrop()` / `_resolveDropSlotState()` (field-collection gate) and `_collectDrop()`.
- `src/scenes/core/dropLayer.ts` — `drawNextDrop()` gated draw.
- `src/powerups/choice.ts` — `buildChoiceCandidates()` hold-full gating.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — `openMiniBossReward()` unlock filter, `openMineralChoice()`, `_restoreCheckpoint()` (resume surface audit), `_telemetryExtras()` (permanent levels in telemetry).
- `src/scenes/core/sceneSetup.ts` — capture/gym loadout application (audit or document divergence).
- `src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts` — `getTempPowerUpIds()` / `clearTemporary()` interaction with the temporary-window rule.
- `src/entities/Player.ts` — `getWeaponLevels()` / `getTempWeaponIds()` and `tickWeaponTimers()`.
- `src/telemetry/schema.ts`, `src/scenes/core/runTelemetry.ts`, `scripts/record-session.mjs` — the recording evidence path for AC1.
- `src/powerups/slots.test.ts`, `src/powerups/slots.parity.test.ts`, `src/ui/HUD.test.ts` — existing coverage to extend.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` §4.4, `docs/BALANCING.md` — cap semantics and HUD presentation docs.

## Related work

- **Limit the number of powerup slots** (AH-0MVLIJT3M005HPHF) — the parent feature that introduced the shared cap; its ACs define the semantics this report must not break.
- **Shared six-slot helper, cap constant and exemption flag** (AH-0MVNT2TEK001BNQ4) — `src/powerups/slots.ts` and `POWER_UP_SLOT_CAP`.
- **Temporary-inclusive six-slot cap with blocked-collection cue** (AH-0MVRCF584004SQFV) — Q4a/Q5b semantics.
- **Gate the shared drop draw on the six-slot pool** (AH-0MVNT2YGD003N8NR), **Gate choice candidates at full slots** (AH-0MVNT2ZXK009Z5VU), **Test drop gating at full slots and below-cap parity** (AH-0MVNT2XHB000YR2Z), **Test the six-slot accounting and exemption flag** (AH-0MVNT2SD300874CP), **Test hold-full choice gating at full slots** (AH-0MVNT2Z89005OPKJ) — the shipped gate and its coverage.
- **Document the six-slot cap and exemption flag** (AH-0MVNT31C50065EE0) — the docs this change must keep true.
- **F7: Document the per-upgrade TTL rule** (AH-0MVUGI5P2001C1IL, completed; parent AH-0MVSTKGC3003OMAC) — the most recent change to the temporary-hold semantics, shipped in commit `bd921d28`; the prime regression suspect for countdown-row behaviour.
- **F4: Permanent grant never strands a temporary stack** (AH-0MVUGI4IC006PUS5, completed) — the companion invariant (a permanent grant clears the weapon's temporary stacks); AC2's mixed-loadout invariant must keep both rules true.
- **When continuing HUD upgrades list is empty** (AH-0MVSHI07B003BZIP, completed) — established that the HUD renders `EffectsRegistry` state, not the player's level store; the same seam makes rows and slots independently derived.
- **On the hull-full upgrade screen show current upgrades** (AH-0MVCRKAPL000L68Y, open) — the choice-overlay surface, not the HUD list; keep separate.
- **Scripted scenes for video** (AH-0MVPJ3NSK008V5VB, completed) and **Scripted-scene setup adoption in every gym scene** (AH-0MVRMHYJR000Y9H8, completed) — the capture-setup surface (`sceneSetup.ts`) that applies loadouts outside the cap.
- **Make weapons both cumulative and time out** (AH-0MTV7RITM009LJF6), **Power-up/weapon leveling + merge rules** (AH-0MUV5CLVO002ZHS9, AH-0MUX802450085VZZ) — the level model the snapshots come from.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption (needs confirmation at review, not blocking intake):** the report is from a `dev` build that contains the cap (shipped 29–30 Oct). If the operator's build predates it, the report is expected behaviour of the older build and this item closes as "already fixed in `dev`".
- **Assumption:** the mixed permanent/countdown rows the operator saw include at least one non-slot row (Mystery UFO or residual Phase Shift/Teleport charges); if instead all seven rows are slot-counted, a real bypass exists and AC2 becomes the primary fix.
- **Risk — HUD layout/legibility:** adding a slot budget or exempt marker changes row density; verify with `src/ui/HUD.test.ts` and an operator screenshot before/after.
- **Risk — capture/gym breakage:** gating `sceneSetup.ts` could break scripted video beats; prefer a documented divergence there over a silent bypass.
- **Risk — temporary-window regressions:** touching `clearTemporary`/`tickWeaponTimers` can resurrect the "temporary pickup never expires" class of bug; the per-upgrade TTL guards (`src/powerups/perUpgradeTtlDocs.test.ts`, `src/powerups/slots.weaponLevels.test.ts`) must stay green.
- **Failure mode to expect, not a bug:** if AC1 shows the seventh row is a non-slot row (Mystery UFO / residual charges), the per-surface gate tests in AC2 will pass unchanged — that is the expected outcome, and AC3 (display agreement) becomes the substantive fix. Report the AC1 classification before writing the fix so the two outcomes are not conflated.
- **Assumption:** the operator can supply the `npm run record` JSONL (they offered); if not, AC1 falls back to a scene test that builds a six-kind loadout plus one non-slot row through the real shared seams.
- **Scope-creep risk:** re-balancing the six-slot cap, changing which entries are exempt, adding per-kind slot weights, or redesigning the HUD are out of scope — record them as `discovered-from:AH-0MVVF0POV001JNKX` items instead.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 — Where did you observe more than six?** — Answer (operator, 2026-10-30): "certainly (a) the in-game HUD upgrade list, probably (c) a seventh item actually functioning." Source: interactive reply. Consequence: the HUD list is the confirmed observation surface; "functioning" is unverified, so a genuine gate bypass must still be ruled out (AC1/AC2).
- **Q2 — Which items were listed / what did the rows show?** — Answer (operator): "both permanent and countdowns" — i.e. the list mixes `∞` permanent rows with timed rows, and no exact row list was supplied. Source: interactive reply. Consequence: countdown rows are temporary-held kinds, which the cap counts, so a seventh row is likely a non-counted row (exempt entry or residual charge pool) or a real bypass; AC1 requires the exact classification from a recording.
- **Q3 — How did the run start?** — Answer (operator): "(a) fresh New Game." Source: interactive reply. Consequence: checkpoint resume is not the observed surface, though it stays in the audit for completeness (AC2).
- **Q — Does the game record logs we could capture the breach with?** — Answer (agent, code evidence): yes. `npm run record` runs `scripts/record-session.mjs`, which starts the dev server with `VITE_TELEMETRY_ENABLED=true VITE_TELEMETRY_SINK=jsonl` and writes the run to a JSONL file: `run_header`, per-tick state including permanent weapon/power-up levels (`PlayScene._telemetryExtras()`), and discrete `pickup` / `hold_full` / `choice_selected` events (`src/telemetry/schema.ts`, `src/scenes/core/runTelemetry.ts`, `docs/TELEMETRY.md`). The operator offered to capture a session; that recording (or a scene test) is the AC1 evidence.
- **Q — Is the cap already enforced, i.e. is this a display bug?** — Answer (agent, code evidence): the shared gate is present and consumed on every normal-play acquisition surface (draw, collection, hold-full choice, mini-boss unlock), and temporary stacks are counted while their window is open. The HUD, however, renders `EffectsRegistry` visibility rules, not `resolveSlotState()`, and has no ceiling, so it can legitimately list more rows than there are slots (Mystery UFO is slot-exempt; Phase Shift/Teleport rows survive a temporary-level expiry via their charge pools; a Teleport arrival opens a Phase Shift row). Source: `src/ui/HUD.ts` L296–L330, L442–L530; `src/powerups/slots.ts`; `src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts` (Resolved decision 1b). **OPEN QUESTION (presentation choice, settle at review):** should non-slot rows be marked (`always available` / exempt), grouped separately, or replaced by an explicit `n/6` slot budget? Agent recommendation: an explicit slot budget plus a distinct marker for exempt/non-slot rows — it makes the cap legible without removing information the player relies on (Mystery UFO availability, recharging charges).
- **Q — Is this a duplicate of an existing item?** — Answer (worklog search + `wl show`): no. Reviewed the six-slot parent and its children (AH-0MVLIJT3M005HPHF, AH-0MVNT2TEK001BNQ4, AH-0MVRCF584004SQFV, AH-0MVNT2YGD003N8NR, AH-0MVNT2ZXK009Z5VU, AH-0MVNT2XHB000YR2Z, AH-0MVNT2SD300874CP, AH-0MVNT2Z89005OPKJ, AH-0MVNT31C50065EE0) and the HUD/choice items above; none reports an over-cap loadout or a HUD/slot-model mismatch.

# Recorder silently loses a session when the browser is closed instead of Ctrl+C

**Issue type:** bug · **Priority:** medium · **Reported:** 2026-10-30 (operator, dev tooling) · **Discovered-from:** AH-0MVVF0POV001JNKX

**Headline:** `npm run record` keeps the whole run's telemetry in the page's in-memory buffer and only writes it after the wait loop exits cleanly, so closing the browser window instead of pressing Ctrl+C throws `Target page, context or browser has been closed` from `page.waitForTimeout`, exits non-zero with a raw Playwright error, and writes **nothing** — a long human session is unrecoverable. Make an interrupted recording recoverable (a crash-safe partial capture) or at minimum fail with one actionable line naming the file that was not written and the correct stop procedure, and state the stop requirement (and the `npm run record -- --auto` separator form) in the tool's usage text and docs.

## Problem statement

`scripts/record-session.mjs` starts Vite with `VITE_TELEMETRY_ENABLED=true VITE_TELEMETRY_SINK=jsonl`, launches Chromium, and polls `readRunEndedSignal` in a `while (!stop.requested)` loop with `page.waitForTimeout(options.pollMs)`. The run's telemetry lives **only** in the page's in-memory buffer, exposed through the dev-gated `window.__aiHellTelemetry` accessor (telemetry never uses `localStorage`, AH-0MVIRYGD1000JVY3). The buffer is drained to disk — `resolveRecordingOutputPath` → `writeFileSync` — **after** the loop. Two consequences:

- **Browser close or page crash mid-recording loses everything.** The `waitForTimeout` (or the next `page.evaluate`) throws a target-closed Playwright error; `main()`'s rejection handler prints the raw message (`page.waitForTimeout: Target page, context or browser has been closed`) and exits 1. No recording is written, no path is named, and nothing tells the operator that the session is gone or how to avoid it next time.
- **The stop procedure is unstated where it is needed.** `--help` lists `[--auto]` and the docs mention Ctrl+C, but neither the usage text nor the failure path says "closing the browser loses the session; press Ctrl+C in the terminal to save". Related: `npm run record --auto` does not reach the script as a flag (npm consumes it) — the working form is `npm run record -- --auto` — and nothing in the tool's own output says so.

This item is the dev-tooling behaviour on a **local** recording. Page-side streaming of telemetry to the dev server (which would bound the loss at one batch by uploading during the run) is a separate, parked item — see the boundary in *Related work*.

## Users

- **Developer / operator running a human session** — "As a developer, when I record a long human session and I close the browser window (or the page crashes) instead of pressing Ctrl+C, I want whatever was captured to be saved, or at least to be told in one line which file was not written and how to record properly next time — I do not want to discover after an hour of play that the recording is gone."
- **Developer reading the tooling** — "As a developer, I want `npm run record --help` and the recording docs to state the stop procedure (Ctrl+C saves; closing the window does not) and the correct `--auto` invocation, so the mistake is avoidable in the first place."
- **Maintainer of the recording tooling** — "As a maintainer, I want the interruption path to be a testable seam (injected page/fs), so the crash path cannot regress into a raw Playwright stack again."

## Existing state (verified in code, `dev` @ 59d40269a)

- `scripts/record-session.mjs`
  - `main()` builds the output path **after** the loop (`resolveRecordingOutputPath(options.output, options)`) — so even the would-be filename does not exist at crash time; the default name is stamped at write time, not at start time.
  - Poll loop: `while (!stop.requested) { decoded = decodeRunEndedDetail(await page.evaluate(readRunEndedSignal)); if (decoded !== null && options.auto) break; if (Date.now() - startedAt >= options.maxDurationMs) break; await page.waitForTimeout(options.pollMs); }`.
  - `createStopController()` handles SIGINT/SIGTERM only — there is no `page.on('close')`, `page.on('crash')` or `browser.on('disconnected')` listener, and no distinction between stop reasons.
  - The buffer is read once, after the loop, through `readDevTelemetryBufferInChunks` (bounded CDP messages).
  - `finally` closes the browser/server; the loop's target-closed error escapes to the top-level handler, which prints `error.message` and `process.exit(1)`.
  - Usage text (`--help`) mentions `[--auto]` but not the Ctrl+C-to-save requirement nor the `npm run record -- --auto` separator form.
- Reusable seams already in `scripts/capture-gameplay.mjs`: `readDevTelemetryChunk({ offset, chunkChars })` returns `{ total, chunk }` — a bounded, incremental slice reader with buffer-reset detection — and `readDevTelemetryBufferInChunks` shows the "total changed ⇒ discard the partial read" rule. Both are plain exported functions, so an incremental checkpoint can reuse them without new page-side code.
- Precedent for the failure UX: `scripts/capture-salvage.mjs` (`salvageFailedCapture`, `formatSalvageMessage`) prints **one** actionable line first (what failed, bytes salvaged, the `.partial.webm` path, next action) and exits non-zero; `scripts/capture-chunk-sink.mjs` writes to `<stem>.partial.webm` and renames into place only on success. The recording tool has no equivalent.
- Docs to keep true: `docs/dev/recording-and-replay.md` §1 (flag table; "On Ctrl+C the tool still exports whatever the sink has already flushed … so an interrupted run yields a partial but valid recording" — true only for Ctrl+C, not for a browser close), and `docs/TELEMETRY.md` L117–122 / L566–574 (the recorder reads the buffer through `window.__aiHellTelemetry`).
- Test coverage today: `scripts/recording-cli.test.ts` covers argument parsing, path resolution, the balance artifact and the `--help`/argv entry guard; `scripts/recording.test.ts` covers the pure recording library. **Nothing** exercises `main()`'s wait loop, the stop reasons, or the browser-close path — `main()` is not reachable without a real browser, which is why the crash path is untested.
- Not covered by this item: the page already POSTs the run to `POST /api/telemetry/upload` at run end (`PlayScene._finishRun()`), so a run that **ended** before the window was closed is already stored server-side; the loss is confined to a run closed mid-run.

## Desired change

1. **Crash-safe partial capture (recommended).** Resolve the output path **before** the browser launches. While recording, checkpoint the page buffer to a documented partial file next to it (`<output>.partial.jsonl`) on an interval (`--checkpoint-ms`, default 15 000 ms, `0` disables), appending **only new bytes** through the incremental `readDevTelemetryChunk` offset loop, and restarting from offset 0 when the reported `total` shrinks (the game started a new run — never mix two runs in one file, mirroring `readDevTelemetryBufferInChunks`). On a clean stop (Ctrl+C, run end, `--max-duration`) write the final file exactly as today and remove the partial. On a browser close / page crash, finalise the partial as the salvaged session and print one actionable line naming it.
2. **Actionable failure when nothing was captured.** If no bytes were captured (or the buffer is unreachable), print exactly one actionable first line — `Recording lost: the browser was closed before Ctrl+C — run npm run record and press Ctrl+C to save` — naming the resolved output path that was **not** written and the correct stop procedure, and exit non-zero. A raw Playwright target-closed message must never be the only diagnostic.
3. **Usage and docs.** `--help` and the docs state: press Ctrl+C in the terminal to finish and save; closing the browser window ends the recording and (at best) salvages a partial file; `--auto` must be passed after `--` (`npm run record -- --auto`).
4. **A testable seam.** Extract the wait/finalise logic into exported, injectable functions (page `evaluate`, fs writes, clock) so the crash, salvage and clean-stop paths are covered hermetically in `scripts/record-session.test.ts` — no real browser in the suite.

**Recorded design decisions (settle at review if the producer prefers otherwise; none blocks intake):**

- **D1 — Local checkpoint, not page streaming.** The fix stays inside `scripts/` (CLI-side). Streaming telemetry to the dev server mid-run is AH-0MVJUAADW0033QBD and is out of scope; if that lands first, this item's checkpoint becomes redundant and the salvage message can point at the server-side partial (a follow-up, not part of this work).
- **D2 — Salvage-then-message, not message-only.** The item's own AC1 allows either branch; the recommendation is to implement both, so a long session is actually recoverable and the message path still covers "nothing captured".
- **D3 — Partial path.** `<resolved output>.partial.jsonl` (e.g. `recordings/session-2026-10-30T21-18-30-585Z.jsonl.partial.jsonl`), inside the already-gitignored `recordings/`. A salvage must never overwrite an existing final recording — use a collision-safe name (numeric suffix) if the target exists, mirroring the dev-upload plugin's collision-safe storage.
- **D4 — No balance artifact for a salvaged partial.** `balance-stats.json` is written only for a clean stop; a salvaged partial is an interrupted run, not a completed one, and the message says so.
- **D5 — Exit codes.** `0` on a clean stop; `1` (non-zero) on an interrupted/crashed recording, whether salvaged or lost — parity with `capture-salvage`.
- **D6 — Default filename stamp becomes the start time.** Resolving the path up front is required for the partial path; the only visible effect is that the default `session-<timestamp>.jsonl` stamp names when recording started.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Browser close mid-recording never silently discards the session.** When the page/browser closes (or crashes) during the wait loop, the recorder writes whatever telemetry had been captured — at least the last checkpointed records, each a complete newline-terminated record that parses through the existing recording reader (`parseTelemetryJsonl` / `parseRecording`), never a half-written line — to the documented partial path (`<output>.partial.jsonl`, collision-safe) and prints **one** actionable line naming that path and the Ctrl+C stop procedure; when nothing was captured it prints exactly one actionable line — `Recording lost: the browser was closed before Ctrl+C — run npm run record and press Ctrl+C to save` — naming the resolved output path that was not written. No Playwright target-closed message is the only diagnostic, and the process exits non-zero. On a clean stop (Ctrl+C / run end / `--max-duration`) the final recording is byte-identical to today's output, no partial file remains, and the exit code is unchanged.
2. **The interruption path is covered by hermetic tests.** New tests (`scripts/record-session.test.ts`, node environment, no real browser — page/fs/clock injected) prove: (a) a target-closed error thrown from the poll loop routes to the salvage path and not to a raw error exit; (b) with zero captured bytes the lost message names the output path and the Ctrl+C procedure; (c) a clean stop writes the final file and removes the partial; (d) the checkpoint appends only new bytes and restarts at offset 0 when the reported buffer `total` shrinks (no two-run mixing); (e) a salvage never overwrites an existing final recording. `scripts/recording-cli.test.ts` keeps passing, extended where it asserts the usage text.
3. **Usage text and docs state the stop requirement.** `npm run record --help` (and `node scripts/record-session.mjs --help`) states the Ctrl+C-to-save requirement, that closing the browser window does not save a completed recording (at best a partial), and the `npm run record -- --auto` separator form; asserted by a test on the help output.
4. **Documentation.** `docs/dev/recording-and-replay.md` §1 (flag table + the Ctrl+C paragraph) and the recorder paragraphs in `docs/TELEMETRY.md` document the partial path, partial-vs-final semantics, the salvage/lost behaviour, the checkpoint flag and the stop procedure. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
5. **Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Constraints

- **Scope ladder.** Only `scripts/record-session.mjs`, a new `scripts/record-session.test.ts`, small additions to `scripts/recording-cli.test.ts` and the two docs above (+ a `.d.mts` update if a new export needs it). **No** changes under `src/`, no new page-side API, no dev-server/upload-protocol change (AH-0MVJUAADW0033QBD), no change to the telemetry schema.
- **Reuse the bounded read seams.** Checkpoint and final reads go through `readDevTelemetryChunk` / `readDevTelemetryBufferInChunks` — never a whole-buffer single CDP message (the string-size overflow class is AH-0MVNVGP55002G0KH).
- **Preserve the clean path.** Ctrl+C, `--auto`, `--max-duration`, `--poll`, `--seed`, `--bot`, `--bot-config`, `--json` and the `balance-stats.json` artifact behave exactly as today; the printed success output keeps its current lines (a salvaged/lost line is additive).
- **Bounded I/O on long runs.** The checkpoint must be append-only and incremental: no per-tick full re-read of the buffer, and no unbounded in-process buffering of the recording. Append only up to the last newline in each chunk (never a partial record), carrying the remainder into the next read.
- **No tracked data writes.** Recordings and partials stay under `recordings/` (gitignored); tests write only into `mkdtempSync` temp dirs, so the suite never dirties the checkout (suite-write guard, AH-0MVS9TY0N0034LZT).
- **Repository boundaries.** Do not edit `.pi/`, `skill/`, `command/` or other agent infrastructure.
- **No new runtime dependency.** Node built-ins plus the already-imported Playwright/Vite modules only.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `scripts/record-session.mjs` — `main()`, `createStopController()`, `resolveRecordingOutputPath()`, `resolveBalanceStatsOutputPath()`, the `--help` block; resolve the output up front, add stop reasons, the checkpoint writer, the salvage/lost finaliser and the `--checkpoint-ms` flag.
- `scripts/record-session.test.ts` *(new)* — hermetic tests for the wait loop / stop reasons / checkpoint / salvage seam with injected page, fs and clock.
- `scripts/recording-cli.test.ts` — existing CLI and `--help` assertions; extend for the new usage lines.
- `scripts/record-session.d.mts` — type surface for any newly exported helper.
- `scripts/capture-gameplay.mjs` — `readDevTelemetryChunk()` / `readDevTelemetryBufferInChunks()` (reused, not modified).
- `scripts/capture-salvage.mjs`, `scripts/capture-chunk-sink.mjs` — the salvage/partial-write precedent to mirror (pattern reference).
- `docs/dev/recording-and-replay.md` §1 — flag table and the Ctrl+C paragraph.
- `docs/TELEMETRY.md` L117–122, L566–574 — the recorder's buffer-read description.

## Related work

- **Crash resilience: incremental telemetry upload so a mid-run reload loses at most one batch** (AH-0MVJUAADW0033QBD, **open**, low, feature) — the page→dev-server streaming item, parked. **Boundary:** it changes when the *server* has the data; this item changes what the *CLI* does when the page dies. Its AC3 requires `record-session` behaviour to stay unchanged, so the two must agree: this item's partial path is local (`recordings/*.partial.jsonl`) and must not touch the upload protocol; if AH-0MVJUAADW0033QBD ships first it supersedes D1/D2 and this item reduces to the message + docs ACs (record that in the work item when it happens).
- **Dev recording, analysis and replay/ghost tooling** (AH-0MUY08W7Y004GATZ, completed) — the parent tooling feature this recorder belongs to; its AC1/AC6 define the buffer-read path.
- **Graceful failure with salvage of streamed bytes** (AH-0MVNT29MC008BQPY, completed) and **Stream recorder chunks to disk through a bounded sink** (AH-0MVNT26AQ005LDNS, completed) — the capture tool's salvage precedent and `.partial.*` naming this fix mirrors.
- **Capture crashes on long full-run clips: Playwright CDP pipe overflows** (AH-0MVN06MS9007LRKE, completed) and **Cap the dev upload message size** (AH-0MVNVGP55002G0KH, completed) — why every buffer read goes through the bounded chunk loop.
- **In-memory dev telemetry sink (no `localStorage`)** (AH-0MVIRYGD1000JVY3, completed) — why a closed page loses the run outright instead of leaving a storage copy behind.
- **Dev-mode telemetry upload with automatic evaluation** (AH-0MVBHRLY8004BGDN, completed) / **docs slice** (AH-0MVBMRR4R004UOLH, completed) — the run-end upload that already stores a *completed* run server-side; the gap is only the mid-run close.
- **Bug: `npm run record` fails with `Unknown argument: /usr/bin/node`** (AH-0MV2RY8XT007I91E, completed) — the argv entry guard and the `--help` assertions in `scripts/recording-cli.test.ts` this item extends.
- **Record tool emits human balance report** (AH-0MV8ISOLG004KPE6, completed) — the `balance-stats.json` artifact whose clean-stop-only rule D4 keeps.
- **Loadout can exceed the six-slot cap** (AH-0MVVF0POV001JNKX, in progress) — the item whose `npm run record` evidence-gathering surfaced this bug (discovered-from).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk — checkpoint cost on long runs.** Reading and appending the buffer every interval adds CDP round-trips and disk writes; the incremental offset keeps it to "new bytes only", but measure a 30-minute recording before merging. Mitigation: default `--checkpoint-ms 15000`, `0` disables, and the final read still uses the existing whole-buffer chunked reader.
- **Risk — mixed runs in one partial.** A run restart resets the page buffer; the checkpoint must honour the `total`-shrink rule (restart at 0, and note the reset in the message) or a partial could concatenate two runs. Covered by AC2(d).
- **Risk — target-closed detection is stringly.** Playwright's error messages vary by version and surface (`page.waitForTimeout`, `page.evaluate`, `browser.newPage`). Mitigation: match the known target-closed message family **and** consult `page.isClosed()` / `browser.isConnected()`; default an unknown failure to the salvage-then-report path rather than a raw stack.
- **Risk — leftover partials.** Partials accumulate in `recordings/` (gitignored) when a session is salvaged; the salvage message names the file, and a salvaged partial is never silently renamed over an existing recording.
- **Risk — breaking the clean path.** Touching the write path could rename or relocate the default output; AC1 requires byte-identical output on a clean stop, and `scripts/recording-cli.test.ts` keeps the path-resolution assertions green.
- **Assumption (A1, observed):** under this repo's npm, `npm run record --auto` does not raise `EUNKNOWNCONFIG`; npm consumes the flag and the script runs a normal wait-for-Ctrl+C recording (`node scripts/record-session.mjs`), i.e. the operator sees an "auto" run that never auto-stops. Under other npm versions the reported `EUNKNOWNCONFIG` appears instead. Either way the fix is usage/docs text plus an actionable line — **not** a change to npm behaviour.
- **Assumption (A2):** the lost session was a headed human recording closed mid-run (no run end), so the dev-server run-end upload never fired and nothing survived server-side.
- **Assumption (A3):** losing at most the last checkpoint interval (~15 s of play) is an acceptable salvage bound; the producer may tune the default.
- **Assumption (A4):** resolving the output path at start time (D6) is acceptable — the visible change is the default filename's timestamp.
- **Scope-creep risk:** page-side autosave/streaming (AH-0MVJUAADW0033QBD), a resume/merge tool for partials, telemetry schema changes, or a `recordings/` janitor are out of scope — record them as `discovered-from:AH-0MVVH57LL00038WQ` items instead.
- **Type and priority rationale:** kept as `bug` (the tool currently behaves incorrectly — it exits with a raw Playwright error and writes nothing) at `medium` — the loss is confined to locally generated dev telemetry that is conveniently re-recordable, so it is neither a broken build nor product data loss (`critical`), nor a blocker of other work (`high`).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q — Where does the recording live, and why is it lost when the browser closes?** — Answer (agent, code evidence): the run lives only in the page's in-memory buffer (`window.__aiHellTelemetry`), and `scripts/record-session.mjs` writes it after the wait loop, so a closed page has nothing to read; the loop's `page.waitForTimeout` throws a target-closed error that escapes to the top-level handler. Source: `scripts/record-session.mjs` L~300–360; `docs/TELEMETRY.md` L117–122; `scripts/capture-gameplay.mjs` `readDevTelemetryBufferInChunks`.
- **Q — Is the session recoverable some other way (server-side upload, `localStorage`)?** — Answer (agent, code evidence): no for a mid-run close. The dev upload (`POST /api/telemetry/upload`) fires only at run end (`PlayScene._finishRun()`), and telemetry never uses `localStorage` (AH-0MVIRYGD1000JVY3), so a page closed mid-run leaves nothing on disk or on the server. A run that *ended* before the window was closed is already stored as `recordings/session-<timestamp>.jsonl` by the upload plugin.
- **Q — Does a salvage/partial precedent exist in this repo?** — Answer (agent, code evidence): yes, for video capture — `scripts/capture-chunk-sink.mjs` writes `<stem>.partial.webm` and renames on success; `scripts/capture-salvage.mjs` emits one actionable first line (failure, bytes, path, next action) and exits non-zero (AH-0MVNT26AQ005LDNS, AH-0MVNT29MC008BQPY). The recording tool has no equivalent; mirroring the pattern keeps the tooling consistent.
- **Q — Is this a duplicate of an existing item?** — Answer (worklog search: `recorder`, `telemetry`, `browser closed`, `waitForTimeout`, `lost recording`, `partial recording`, `Ctrl+C`): no full duplicate. **Partial overlap** with **Crash resilience: incremental telemetry upload so a mid-run reload loses at most one batch** (AH-0MVJUAADW0033QBD, open, low) — that item streams batches page→dev-server and explicitly requires `record-session` behaviour to stay unchanged. This brief was scoped to the **CLI-local** loss/UX (checkpoint + salvage + message + usage/docs) and records the boundary and supersession rule under *Related work*.
- **Q — What exactly happens today with `npm run record --auto`?** — Answer (agent, reproduced 2026-10-31 on this checkout): it starts Vite and the recorder and runs a normal wait-for-Ctrl+C session (`node scripts/record-session.mjs`, npm consuming `--auto`); the reported `EUNKNOWNCONFIG` did not reproduce under this npm version. Source: local run output. Consequence: AC3 documents `npm run record -- --auto`; no npm behaviour change is attempted.
- **OPEN QUESTION (non-blocking, presentation/behaviour choice for review) — salvage a partial, or fail with a message only?** — AC1 accepts either. **Recommended:** checkpoint + salvage with the message as the nothing-captured fallback — it makes an hour-long human session recoverable instead of merely explained, and it mirrors the capture tool's existing salvage idiom (D2). The message-only branch alone satisfies AC1 and is a much smaller change if the producer prefers the minimum.
- **OPEN QUESTION (non-blocking) — checkpoint interval default.** **Recommended:** `--checkpoint-ms 15000` (at most ~15 s of play lost, one CDP round-trip per interval, append-only). The producer may choose a tighter/looser default or ship it disabled by default.

### Related work items
- **AH-0MVJUAADW0033QBD** – Crash resilience: incremental telemetry upload so a mid-run reload loses at most one batch (open)

## Goal

As a maintainer, I want an automated guard that the HUD upgrade list and the shared six-slot model cannot drift, plus a committed fixture that reproduces the reported ">6 equipped" reading — so the display fix (child F2) is driven by a failing test, not by inspection.

## Context (evidence from AH-0MVVF0POV001JNKX)

RCA over `recordings/six-slot.jsonl` (runSeed 3596032192) showed the cap is enforced but `HUD.refresh()` renders rows per visible `EffectsRegistry` state, not per slot:

- **tick 4540** — 6 slot-counted kinds held (`heavy_slug, mineral_scoop, mortar, rapid, shard_swarm, strike`) but only **5 rows**, because a field-pickup Strike renders no row (`_isPowerUpRowVisible('strike')` → `isStrikePermanent()`).
- **tick 5899** — **7 rows** for 5 slots: 5 slot-counted (`heavy_slug, mortar, spread` permanent + `rear_guard, salvage` temp) plus `mystery_ufo` (slot-exempt `availableWhenSlotsFull`, producer Q7a) and `phase_shift` (residual charges after its 15 s temporary window expired, producer Resolved decision 1b).

The recording itself is gitignored (`recordings/`), so the test needs a small committed fixture carrying only the ids/levels/windows that matter.

## Scope

- A compact fixture (JSON or inline table) encoding those two states plus one ordinary below-cap mixed loadout.
- HUD-level tests asserting: slot-counted rows == `resolveSlotState().used`; never > `POWER_UP_SLOT_CAP`; non-slot rows (exempt entry, charge-pool residue) are classified as non-slot.
- A model invariant test: any mixed permanent + temporary loadout yields `used <= POWER_UP_SLOT_CAP`.
- Tests must **fail on the current code** (the 7-rows/5-slots case) and pass once child F2 lands.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Fixture.** A committed fixture (or inline fixture builder) reproduces the three loadouts above through the real shared seams (`PowerUpLevelStore`, `Player.equipWeapon`/`collectWeapon` equivalents, `EffectsRegistry`), documented with a comment tying it to the RCA ticks (4540, 5899) and the work item id; no dependency on `recordings/`.
2. **Agreement test.** A test asserts, for each loadout, that the number of HUD rows whose kind is slot-counted equals `resolveSlotState(...).used` and is `<= POWER_UP_SLOT_CAP`; the 7-row/5-slot case fails on current code (red test demonstrated on the branch before F2 lands).
3. **Non-slot classification.** A test asserts the exempt Mystery UFO row and a residual Phase Shift/Teleport charge row are treated as non-slot (excluded from the slot-counted row count) regardless of whether they are displayed.

## Goal

As a player, I want the upgrade list to show how much of the six-slot loadout I am using and to distinguish upgrades that do **not** consume a slot, so the list never looks like I am carrying seven items when the ship holds five or six.

## Context

RCA (AH-0MVVF0POV001JNKX): the cap is enforced, but `HUD.refresh()` renders one row per visible `EffectsRegistry` state (`_buildPowerUpRows` / `_isPowerUpRowVisible` + `activeWeapons()`). Two row classes never hold a slot — the `availableWhenSlotsFull` exempt entries (Mystery UFO; Extra Life has no row) and Phase Shift/Teleport charge-pool rows that survive a temporary-window expiry (producer Resolved decision 1b) — while a temporary one-shot like Strike holds a slot but renders no row at all. Observed live: 7 rows for 5 slots (tick 5899) and 5 rows for 6 slots (tick 4540) in `recordings/six-slot.jsonl`.

## Scope

Make the HUD present the slot budget and mark non-slot rows, derived from the **single shared helper** `resolvePlayerSlotState(player)` (`src/powerups/slots.ts`) — no second occupancy counter and no slot arithmetic in the HUD.

- A slot budget readout (for example `Loadout 5/6`) rendered with the existing rows, hidden or inert when there is no player/registry.
- Non-slot rows visibly marked: exempt entries (Mystery UFO) as always-available, and charge-only Phase Shift/Teleport rows as charge pools rather than slot-holders. Exact visual treatment (label suffix, icon tint, grouping) is settled at review; the requirement is that a player can tell which six entries are the loadout.
- Slot state reaches the HUD through one shared seam supplied by the scene (game and gyms alike), not by re-deriving occupancy per scene.
- No behaviour change below the cap and no change to what is spawnable/collectable/offerable.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Budget is correct.** The HUD exposes the current slot occupancy and cap (e.g. `used/cap`), derived only from `resolvePlayerSlotState`; asserting the rendered/read-back value equals `used` and `POWER_UP_SLOT_CAP` for below-cap, exactly-six and >6-row scenarios.
2. **Non-slot rows are distinguishable.** Exempt entries (Mystery UFO) and residual charge-pool rows (Phase Shift/Teleport) are rendered with their non-slot status evident (marker/label/group), and are excluded from the slot-counted row count; asserted by HUD tests.
3. **Slot-counted rows match the model.** For every loadout in the F1 fixture, the HUD's slot-counted rows equal `resolveSlotState().used` and never exceed `POWER_UP_SLOT_CAP`.
4. **Game↔gym parity.** The HUD is shared (`src/ui/HUD.ts`); whatever seam supplies slot state is wired once in the shared scene layer so `PlayScene` and every gym show the identical budget — no per-scene copies (AH-0MUGZDTFX004RBD1).
5. **No gameplay change.** Spawning, collection gating, hold-full/mini-boss offers and temporary TTL behaviour are unchanged; existing power-up/weapon/HUD suites stay green.
6. **Full project test suite must pass with the new changes**, and all related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and the relevant GDD/`docs/BALANCING.md` entries.

- **Parent AC coverage (parent AC3).** **The displayed loadout agrees with the model.** For a mixed permanent + countdown loadout the HUD's slot-counted rows equal `resolveSlotState().used` and never exceed `POWER_UP_SLOT_CAP`; non-slot rows are visibly distinguished from equipped kinds (or replaced by an explicit slot budget). Asserted by a HUD/scene test over a loadout that includes an exempt entry and a residual charge pool.

## Key Files

- `src/ui/HUD.ts` — `refresh()`, `_buildPowerUpRows()`, `_isPowerUpRowVisible()`, `_addRow()`/`_addWeaponRow()`, `_rowY()` (layout), public test accessors.
- `src/powerups/slots.ts` — `resolvePlayerSlotState`, `PowerUpSlotState`, `POWER_UP_SLOT_CAP`.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts` — the shared seam where a scene supplies its player to the HUD (game + gyms).
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` and `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts` — HUD construction points to confirm the single wiring site.
- `src/powerups/effects.ts` — `EffectsRegistry` accessors the rows already use (`powerUpLevel`, `phaseCharges`, `teleportStacks`).
- `src/ui/HUD.test.ts`, `src/ui/__tests__/` — row/budget assertions.
